```mermaid
    REGISTRY["national register of<br/>wallet-relying parties"]
    REG["registrar"]
    ACP["provider of<br/>wallet-relying party<br/>access certificates"]
    RCP["provider of<br/>wallet-relying party<br/>registration certificates"]

    WRP["wallet-relying party"]
    AC["access<br/>certificate"]
    RC["registration<br/>certificate"]
    WEB["Website"]
    API["API"]

    MS -->|"establishes and<br/>maintains at least one"| REGISTRY
    MS -->|"designate at<br/>least one"| REG
    MS -->|"shall authorize at<br/>least one"| ACP

    REG -->|"manage and<br/>operate"| REGISTRY

    WRP -->|"is listed<br/>by"| REGISTRY

    REGISTRY -->|"provides information<br/>about WRPs"| WEB
```

*Figure: Institutional architecture for registration of wallet-relying parties, adapted from ETSI TS 119 475 Figure 1.*

In practice, this architecture makes the responsibility split explicit: the national register remains authoritative, Access CAs use it to issue Service-bound WRPACs, and the Registration Certificate CA automatically projects each registered `(Service, intended use)` pair into its own WRPRC. Wallet presentation requests carry the applicable WRPRC, avoiding a routine Wallet-to-Registrar dependency during the approval ceremony.

> **Architectural Note (Direct vs Intermediated Registration):** The flow later in this chapter represents the **Direct RP Model**, where the Relying Party registers to obtain both Registration Certificates (expressing intended use) and an Access Certificate (for Wallet connection). In the **Intermediary RP Model**, the Intermediary registers to obtain the Access Certificate, while the Intermediated RP registers to obtain Registration Certificates referencing their chosen Intermediary.

ETSI TS 119 475 Annex D describes four institutional arrangements that Member States can combine with national registration policy. CIR 2026/1730 now constrains all of them to the same outcome for an RP: the authorized Registration Certificate CA must issue the Service/intended-use certificates automatically and without undue delay after registration.

| ETSI TS 119 475 Annex D model | Who drives the issuance flow | RP-facing consequence |
|:-------------------|:-----------------------------|:----------------------|
| **Integrated model** | Registrar and certificate provider are the same entity | Registration and certificate issuance are operationally coupled, which simplifies traceability but concentrates issuance responsibilities in one authority. |
| **Registrar-initiated issuance** | Registrar finishes registration and instructs the certificate provider | The RP may never contact the certificate provider directly; issuance timing and triggering remain under registrar control. |
| **RP-initiated post-registration** | RP contacts the certificate provider after registration | A national interface may still let the RP initiate delivery or retrieval, but it cannot turn issuance into an optional manual step or postpone the automatic post-registration outcome. |
| **Provider-assisted registration** | Certificate provider helps collect registration material and proxy the registrar interaction | The RP gets a one-stop onboarding path, but the registrar still governs the authoritative registration outcome and identity basis. |

The direct-flow sequence later in this chapter uses a Registrar-triggered model because it makes the amended legal invariant visible. It is not a mandate for one national API topology. Across all four arrangements, ETSI TS 119 475 clause `4.6.3` keeps the national register as the authoritative source of identity and status attributes, while identity proofing can be performed either by the Registrar itself or by authorized entities acting on its behalf under national registration policy.

For RPs, the practical consequences are:

- A WRPAC provider may perform identity proofing itself, or may rely entirely on registrar-side identity proofing when issuance is triggered from the register workflow.
- A WRPRC does **not** imply a fresh full identity-proofing cycle on every issuance, because WRPRCs are not bound to a signing key pair and may simply reflect updated register data.
- WRPRCs are issued only to the party they pertain to, so certificate possession remains under the control of the designated WRP.
- ETSI TS 119 475 intentionally leaves the EUDIW-to-register API out of scope; the standard only fixes the institutional roles and the RP-visible artifacts, not a single wallet-to-register protocol.

#### 4.2 RP Registration and Certificate Data Model

ARF v3 adds a Service layer to the existing TS2/TS5/TS6 registration record. The result is not one flat `WalletRelyingParty` object with a bag of intended uses; it is an identifier and certificate graph with explicit ownership and cardinality:

| Object or identifier | Created or chosen by | Scope and uniqueness | Certificate/runtime consequence |
|:---------------------|:---------------------|:---------------------|:--------------------------------|
| **EU-wide RP identifier** | Registrar, from verified official identifiers | Stable for the registered entity across the Union | Identical across all WRPACs and WRPRCs for that RP |
| **Service identifier** | RP, then registered by the Registrar | Unique within the RP; may reuse an OAuth `client_id`; a Registrar may permit a placeholder for a one-Service RP | Included with the same Service trade name in all WRPACs and WRPRCs for that Service |
| **Intended-use identifier** | Registrar | Identifies one registered intended use mapped to one Service | Selects one WRPRC for the current Service/use pair |
| **RP Instance identifier** | RP-local operations, if one is needed | No ARF-wide legal identifier is created for an Instance; its key and certificate inventory distinguish the deployment | One Instance may serve multiple Services, but it needs a separate WRPAC for each Service |
| **WRPAC certificate serial/fingerprint** | Access CA | Unique within the issuing PKI | Inventory key for one Instance/Service binding and its delivered signing/intermediate chain |
| **WRPRC `id` and status index** | Registration Certificate CA | Unique within the issuer/status-list system | Inventory key for one `(Service, intended use)` certificate and its lifecycle state |

The deterministic selection rule is: choose the WRPAC whose key is held by the current RP Instance and whose RP/Service identifiers describe the active Service, then include exactly one WRPRC whose RP identifier, Service identifier, Service trade name, and intended use match that request. An Instance serving two Services therefore needs at least two WRPACs; if those Services have two and three intended uses respectively, the RP receives five WRPRCs and distributes only the applicable subset to each Instance.

The standards boundary is equally important:

| Trust artifact | Controlling profile after CIR 2026/1730 | Required binding and policy surfaces |
|:---------------|:------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------|
| **WRPAC** | ETSI TS 119 411-8 V1.1.1, replacing the former generic NCP substitution | RP and Service identifiers/trade names, Instance public key, certificate chain, certificate policy/CPS, national-register reference, and—when the subject is an intermediary—the associated end-RP identifier plus end-RP Service identifier |
| **WRPRC** | ETSI TS 119 475 V1.2.1 | RP and Service identifiers/trade names, precisely one intended use for an RP Service certificate, registered credential/claim scope, general access policy, provider policy/CPS, expiry, and status reference |

The underlying publication model remains split across three EC technical-specification layers:

- **TS2** provides reusable `LegalEntity` and `Provider` structures.
- **TS5** defines the `WalletRelyingParty` publication/API shapes.
- **TS6** identifies the minimum and role-dependent information that Member State registers capture.

Those layers explain what is registered and published. ARF v3 Service semantics and the two ETSI certificate profiles explain how that state is partitioned and carried into wallet-facing trust artifacts.

##### 4.2.1 WalletRelyingParty Data Model

The current registration model is defined in [TS5 §2](https://github.com/eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-doc-standards-and-technical-specifications/blob/b53874f1477a76f00a91c87cfd3f18abea572e65/docs/technical-specifications/ts5-common-formats-and-api-for-rp-registration-information.md#2-data-model), with superclass dependencies on [TS2 §2.1–§3.2](https://github.com/eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-doc-standards-and-technical-specifications/blob/b53874f1477a76f00a91c87cfd3f18abea572e65/docs/technical-specifications/ts2-notification-publication-provider-information.md#21-legalentity). `WalletRelyingParty` inherits from `Provider`, which in turn inherits from `LegalEntity`. Compared with the older TS5 snapshot used in earlier drafts of this article, TS5 v1.3 now makes the supervisory-authority and attestation-provider surfaces explicit via dedicated `SupervisoryAuthority` and `ProvidedAttestation` classes, and it uses current carriage names such as `entitlements`, `credentials`, and `claims`.

The simplified UML below preserves the current TS2/TS5 publication baseline and adds the ARF v3 logical `RelyingPartyService` overlay. Until the external TS5 schema is republished with a concrete Service container, implementations may have to project existing RP-level fields into this logical boundary; they must not flatten away the Service identifier, certificate cardinality, or Service-to-intended-use mapping.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    direction TB

    class LegalEntity {
        legalPerson : LegalPerson [0..1]
        naturalPerson : NaturalPerson [0..1]
        identifier : Identifier [0..*]
        postalAddress : string [0..*]
        country : string [1..1]
        email : string [0..*]

        infoURI : string [0..*]
    }

    }

        isPSB : boolean [1..1]
        entitlements : string [1..*]

        supervisoryAuthority : SupervisoryAuthority [1..1]

        usesIntermediary : WalletRelyingParty [0..*]
        isIntermediary : boolean [1..1]
    }

    class RelyingPartyService {
```

##### 4.2.2 TS6 Mandatory and Role-Dependent Registered Data

TS6 does not redefine the whole class model. Instead, it tells Member States which pieces of the TS2/TS5 registration baseline must always be captured and which appear only for specific RP roles. The tables below preserve TS6's business-level data identifiers, while mapping them to the current TS5 v1.3 attribute names used elsewhere in this document.

**TS6 mandatory registration baseline**

| TS6 data identifier | Current model carriage | Why it matters |
|:--------------------|:-----------------------|:---------------|
| `Name` | `WalletRelyingParty.legalPerson.legalName` or `WalletRelyingParty.naturalPerson.{givenName,familyName}` | The register must expose the official identity of the registered entity, whether it is a legal person or a natural person. |
| `Trade Name` | `WalletRelyingParty.tradeName` plus logical `RelyingPartyService.serviceTradeName` | User-facing RP and Service names when different from the official name. |
| `Identifier` | `WalletRelyingParty.identifier` | At least one official identifier; EUID is the preferred technical anchor where available. |
| `Info URI` | `WalletRelyingParty.infoURI` | Informational/public website surface distinct from support channels. |
| `Physical Address` | `WalletRelyingParty.postalAddress` | Postal establishment address available to the Registrar. |
| `Contact Information` | `WalletRelyingParty.supportURI`, `WalletRelyingParty.phone`, `WalletRelyingParty.email` | At least one support/helpdesk channel for registration- and intended-use-related matters. |
| `Service Description` | Logical `RelyingPartyService.serviceDescription`, projected through `WalletRelyingParty.srvDescription` where the published schema remains flat | Localized description of the applicable RP Service. |
| `Public Sector Body` | `WalletRelyingParty.isPSB` | Distinguishes public-sector bodies from private RPs. |
| `Entitlements` | `WalletRelyingParty.entitlements` | Registered RP role set, later aligned with the ETSI TS 119 475 entitlement URIs. |
| `Purpose` | `RelyingPartyService.intendedUse[].purpose` | Localized explanation of each intended use mapped to that Service. |
| `Data Requested` | `RelyingPartyService.intendedUse[].credentials[]` | Declared attestation formats, metadata, and claim paths for the Service/use pair. |
| `Data Protection Authority` | `WalletRelyingParty.supervisoryAuthority` | DPA contact object supervising the RP and its intended uses. |

**TS6 role-dependent mandatory data**

| TS6 data identifier | Current model carriage | When it becomes mandatory |
|:--------------------|:-----------------------|:--------------------------|
| `Identifier` (additional) | `WalletRelyingParty.identifier` | When alternate identifiers beyond the primary EUID or national unique identifier are registered. |
| `Use of Intermediary` | `WalletRelyingParty.usesIntermediary` | When a service-provider RP relies on one or more intermediaries instead of transacting directly with wallet units. |
| `Is Intermediary` | `WalletRelyingParty.isIntermediary` | When the registered RP itself acts on behalf of other relying parties. |
| `Provides Attestations` | `WalletRelyingParty.providesAttestations` | When the RP is also a QEAA/PuB-EAA/PID/non-qualified EAA provider and must declare which attestations it issues. |

> **RP implementation consequence:** TS7 and TS8 consume this same registration baseline rather than inventing separate data sources. In practice, the registered `supportURI`/email/phone channels drive deletion-request handling, and the registered `supervisoryAuthority` data drives DPA-reporting flows. ETSI TS 119 475 then defines how the same RP-facing information may be carried in WRPRCs and related wallet-visible artifacts.

**Amended CIR Annex I provenance and verification classes**

CIR 2026/1730 changes the evidence meaning of the registration record. Article 6(3)(a) requires the Registrar to verify the accuracy, validity, authenticity, and integrity of points `1–6` and `11–16`. New Article 6(3a) requires points `7–10` to be collected automatically only for transparency, with no preauthorisation process. A policy engine must preserve that distinction:

| Annex I point | Registered information | Evidence class | Safe interpretation |
|:-------------:|:-----------------------|:---------------|:--------------------|
| 1 | Official name and source-record identification data | **Registrar-verified** | Verified legal/natural-person identity input |
| 2 | User-friendly trade or service name | **Registrar-verified** | Verified display identity; must stay consistent across the RP's certificates |
| 3 | Official RP identifiers and their source-record data | **Registrar-verified** | Basis for the Registrar-assigned EU-wide RP identifier |
| 4 | Physical establishment address | **Registrar-verified** | Verified establishment data; not necessarily published in every query response |
| 5 | RP-controlled URL | **Registrar-verified** | Verified registered URL, distinct from intended-use privacy/support metadata |
| 6 | Required Member State country prefix | **Registrar-verified** | Verified identifier-jurisdiction syntax |
| 7 | Helpdesk/support website, phone, or email | **Automatically collected transparency data; no preauthorisation** | Contact channel, not evidence that a purpose or entitlement was approved |
| 8 | Description of the services provided | **Automatically collected transparency data; no preauthorisation** | User-facing description, not an authorization grant |
| 9 | Requested attestations/attributes for each intended use | **Automatically collected transparency data; no preauthorisation** | The registered comparison set for overasking checks, not Registrar approval of legal necessity |
| 10 | Description of each intended use | **Automatically collected transparency data; no preauthorisation** | RP-declared purpose shown to the User; legal basis and proportionality still require RP governance |
| 11 | Public-sector-body indicator | **Registrar-verified** | Verified status/classification input |
| 12 | Entitlement or entitlements | **Registrar-verified** | Verified role entitlement used by certificate and issuance policy |
| 13 | Additional non-qualified EAA sub-entitlements | **Registrar-verified** | Verified national extension of the entitlement set |
| 14 | Indication that the RP uses an intermediary | **Registrar-verified** | Verified intermediary topology flag |
| 15 | Association from an intermediated RP to its intermediary | **Registrar-verified** | Bound in the RP's WRPRC as intermediary identifier plus intermediary Service identifier |
| 16 | Association from an intermediary WRPAC to the end RP | **Registrar-verified** | Bound in the intermediary's access certificate as end-RP identifier plus end-RP Service identifier |

Certificate profiles add **derived or certificate-carried fields** on top of those registered facts. The EU-wide RP identifier is derived from verified official identifiers; the RP-chosen Service identifier, Registrar-created intended-use identifier, Service-to-use mapping, certificate serial/`id`, Instance public key, national-register reference, general access policy, provider policy/CPS, validity window, and revocation/status reference are created or carried by the responsible Registrar or CA. They must not be mislabelled as extra Annex I entitlements.

##### 4.2.2.1 Topic 27 Publication and Access-Certificate Boundary

ARF Topic 27 sharpens the implementation boundary around the TS5/TS6 model: registration data is not merely stored by the Member State; it is published, queryable, change-logged, and used as the eligibility input for access-certificate issuance.

| Topic 27 requirement surface | RP-facing consequence |
|:-----------------------------|:----------------------|
| Member States register a common dataset for PID Providers, QEAA Providers, PuB-EAA Providers, non-qualified EAA Providers, and RPs (`Reg_01`-`Reg_01a`). | Dual-role entities must keep verifier-side RP data and issuer-side provider data coherent, especially where `providesAttestations` declares issued attestation types. |
| Registration-process documentation is public (`Reg_02`). | An RP can evaluate onboarding evidence, appeal/redress expectations, and update obligations before submitting. |
| Registry entries are published online in signed or sealed machine-readable TS5 format and in human-readable form (`Reg_03`-`Reg_04`). | Wallets and auditors can verify registered scope without treating the RP's own backend as the source of truth. |
| Machine-readable and human-readable retrieval must not require authentication or prior registration (`Reg_04`, `Reg_06`). | Public lookup is the transparency path; authenticated administration or update APIs are a separate national concern. |
| Updates must be possible and changes are logged, including registration, updates, deletion, suspension, and cancellation (`Reg_07`-`Reg_09`). | RP systems need registered-data change control and evidence retention, not one-time onboarding screenshots. |
| Relying Party identity proofing is risk-proportionate and explicitly considers intermediary status (`Reg_25`-`Reg_26`). | Intermediary onboarding can receive stronger scrutiny than ordinary low-risk service-provider registration. |
| Access CAs issue one or more access certificates to every registered RP Instance, with a separate certificate for each Service served by that Instance (`Reg_10a`-`Reg_10b`). | WRPAC issuance is mandatory for wallet-facing authentication, but each certificate is an Instance/Service binding rather than the full intended-use authorization record. |
| Access certificates contain the entity trade name and EU-wide identifier plus the applicable Service identifier and Service trade name, consistent with the matching registration certificate(s) (`Reg_31`-`Reg_34`, `RPRC_06`-`RPRC_08`). | Wallets can compare stable RP and Service identity across the two certificate types and detect cross-Service certificate substitution. |

##### 4.2.3 Wallet-Relying Party Roles and Identifiers (ETSI TS 119 475 Annex A)

Once the TS2/TS5/TS6 registration baseline exists, ETSI TS 119 475 Annex A turns the business-level RP roles into stable machine-readable identifiers that can appear in national register data and in the WRPRC `entitlements` field. The top-level entitlement namespace is `id-etsi-wrpa-entitlement` (`0.4.0.19475.1`). These values are not just display labels: wallets can use them as disclosure-control inputs, and users can see them as part of understanding what kind of relying party is requesting data.

| Entitlement | Description | OID form | URI |
|:------------|:------------|:---------|:----|
| `Service_Provider` | General service provider | `id-etsi-wrpa-entitlement 1` | `https://uri.etsi.org/19475/Entitlement/Service_Provider` |
| `QEAA_Provider` | Qualified trust service provider issuing qualified electronic attestations of attributes | `id-etsi-wrpa-entitlement 2` | `https://uri.etsi.org/19475/Entitlement/QEAA_Provider` |
| `Non_Q_EAA_Provider` | Trust service provider issuing non-qualified electronic attestations of attributes | `id-etsi-wrpa-entitlement 3` | `https://uri.etsi.org/19475/Entitlement/Non_Q_EAA_Provider` |
| `PUB_EAA_Provider` | Public sector body or its agent issuing electronic attestations of attributes from authentic sources | `id-etsi-wrpa-entitlement 4` | `https://uri.etsi.org/19475/Entitlement/PUB_EAA_Provider` |
| `PID_Provider` | Provider of person identification data | `id-etsi-wrpa-entitlement 5` | `https://uri.etsi.org/19475/Entitlement/PID_Provider` |
| `QCert_for_ESeal_Provider` | QTSP issuing qualified certificates for electronic seals | `id-etsi-wrpa-entitlement 6` | `https://uri.etsi.org/19475/Entitlement/QCert_for_ESeal_Provider` |
| `QCert_for_ESig_Provider` | QTSP issuing qualified certificates for electronic signatures | `id-etsi-wrpa-entitlement 7` | `https://uri.etsi.org/19475/Entitlement/QCert_for_ESig_Provider` |
| `rQSealCDs_Provider` | QTSP managing remote qualified electronic seal creation devices | `id-etsi-wrpa-entitlement 8` | `https://uri.etsi.org/19475/Entitlement/rQSealCDs_Provider` |
| `rQSigCDs_Provider` | QTSP managing remote qualified electronic signature creation devices | `id-etsi-wrpa-entitlement 9` | `https://uri.etsi.org/19475/Entitlement/rQSigCDs_Provider` |
| `ESig_ESeal_Creation_Provider` | Non-qualified provider for remote signature/seal creation | `id-etsi-wrpa-entitlement 10` | `https://uri.etsi.org/19475/Entitlement/ESig_ESeal_Creation_Provider` |

Most RPs that only consume attributes from Wallet Users register with the single entitlement `Service_Provider`. Dual-role entities that both consume attributes and issue attestations or trust-service outputs may need additional provider entitlements alongside that baseline role.

Annex A also defines a first set of **service-provider sub-entitlements** that are especially relevant for banks and PSPs:

| PSP sub-entitlement | URI |
|:--------------------|:----|
| `Account Servicing Payment Service Provider` | `https://uri.etsi.org/19475/SubEntitlement/psp/psp-as` |
| `Payment Initiation Service Provider` | `https://uri.etsi.org/19475/SubEntitlement/psp/psp-pi` |
| `Account Information Service Provider` | `https://uri.etsi.org/19475/SubEntitlement/psp/psp-ai` |
| `Payment Service Provider issuing card-based payment instruments` | `https://uri.etsi.org/19475/SubEntitlement/psp/psp-ic` |
| `Unspecified Payment Service Provider` | `https://uri.etsi.org/19475/SubEntitlement/psp/unspecified` |

These sub-entitlements matter when a plain `Service_Provider` label is too coarse. They give wallets and relying-party ecosystems a more precise machine-readable role for payment use cases without fragmenting the top-level entitlement vocabulary.

> **Disclosure-control relevance:** ETSI TS 119 475 explicitly treats these roles as inputs to disclosure decisions. In other words, the entitlement set is part of how the wallet ecosystem reasons about whether a relying party should receive a given class of data, not just how the RP is described to humans.

##### 4.2.4 ETSI TS 119 475 Annex B Normative Attribute Model

ETSI TS 119 475 Annex B is the **normative attribute model** behind later WRPAC and WRPRC mappings. The TS2/TS5/TS6 baseline above remains useful as the registration-side inheritance and minimum-data view, but ETSI TS 119 475 Annex B should be treated as the certificate-facing source whenever this document discusses exact field names, multiplicities, and RP-visible semantics.

This matters because Annex B makes several practical distinctions explicit:

- `supportURI` is a mandatory support/deletion-request channel; `infoURI` is a separate transparency/information channel.
- `srvDescription` and `purpose` are multilingual structured values, not single free-text strings.
- Intermediary use is modeled through `usesIntermediary`, not just a generic role label.
- Public-body status, provider-issued attestations, privacy-policy links, and intended-use lifecycle dates are all first-class registration attributes.

ETSI TS 119 475 Annex B also states that these classes are defined for clarity and interoperability, not to prescribe a specific implementation language or storage model.

**Class `WalletRelyingParty` (`B.2.1`)**

| Attribute | Mult. | Type | RP-facing meaning |
|:----------|:-----:|:-----|:------------------|
| `tradeName` | `[0..1]` | `string` | Trade/common/service name shown to users and reused in certificate mappings. |
| `supportURI` | `[1..*]` | `string` | Mandatory support contact channel for the WRP, including at least one route for deletion requests. |
| `srvDescription` | `[1..*]` | `MultiLangString[]` | Localized descriptions of the services provided by the WRP. |
| `intendedUse` | `[0..*]` | `IntendedUse` | Declared use cases for requesting specific attestations from wallets. |
| `isPSB` | `[1..1]` | `boolean` | Indicates whether the WRP is a public sector body. |
| `entitlement` | `[1..*]` | `string` | Annex A role/entitlement identifiers assigned to the WRP. |
| `providesAttestations` | `[0..*]` | `Credential` | Credential descriptions used when the WRP is itself an attestation-issuing/provider role. |
| `supervisoryAuthority` | `[1..1]` | `LegalEntity` | Competent data-protection supervisory authority for the WRP. |
| `registryURI` | `[1..1]` | `string` | National registry API endpoint for this registered WRP. |
| `usesIntermediary` | `[0..*]` | `WalletRelyingParty` | Indicates that the WRP depends on one or more intermediaries. |

> **Implementation consequence:** Annex B models intermediated operation through explicit `usesIntermediary` relationships. It does **not** rely on a standalone `isIntermediary` flag as the primary normative expression of that relationship.

**Class `LegalEntity` (`B.2.2`)**

| Attribute | Mult. | Type | RP-facing meaning |
|:----------|:-----:|:-----|:------------------|
| `legalPerson` | `[0..1]` | `LegalPerson` | Legal-person-specific attributes. Only one of `legalPerson` or `naturalPerson` may be present. |
| `naturalPerson` | `[0..1]` | `NaturalPerson` | Natural-person-specific attributes. Only one of `legalPerson` or `naturalPerson` may be present. |
| `identifier` | `[0..*]` | `Identifier` | Official identifiers anchored in authoritative records. |
| `postalAddress` | `[1..1]` | `string` | Postal address of the entity. |
| `country` | `[1..1]` | `string` | ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, or `EU` for European-level providers. |
| `email` | `[0..*]` | `string` | One or more RFC 5322 email addresses. |
| `phone` | `[0..*]` | `string` | One or more international phone numbers, beginning with `+` and country code. |
| `infoURI` | `[0..*]` | `string` | General-purpose public information pages about the entity. |

> **Support vs information:** Annex B is explicit that `infoURI` complements, but does not replace, the dedicated support channels carried in `supportURI`.

**Class `LegalPerson` (`B.2.3`)**

| Attribute | Mult. | Type | RP-facing meaning |
|:----------|:-----:|:-----|:------------------|
| `legalName` | `[1..*]` | `string` | Official legal name(s) of the legal person as recorded in authoritative records. |
| `establishedBylaw` | `[0..*]` | `Law` | Legal basis by which the legal person is established. |

**Class `NaturalPerson` (`B.2.4`)**

| Attribute | Mult. | Type | RP-facing meaning |
|:----------|:-----:|:-----|:------------------|
| `givenName` | `[1..1]` | `string` | First name(s), including middle names where applicable. |
| `familyName` | `[1..1]` | `string` | Last name(s) or surnames. |
| `dateOfBirth` | `[0..1]` | `string` | Date of birth from official records. |
| `placeOfBirth` | `[0..1]` | `string` | Place of birth from official records. |

**Class `Identifier` (`B.2.5`)**

| Attribute | Mult. | Type | RP-facing meaning |
|:----------|:-----:|:-----|:------------------|
| `type` | `[1..1]` | `string` | URI-identified identifier scheme. ETSI TS 119 475 defines at least `EORI-No`, `LEI`, `EUID`, `VATIN`, `TIN`, and `Excise`; additional national/EU types may also exist. |
| `identifier` | `[1..1]` | `string` | Concrete identifier value for the `LegalEntity`. |

**Class `MultiLangString` (`B.2.6`)**

| Attribute | Mult. | Type | RP-facing meaning |
|:----------|:-----:|:-----|:------------------|
| `lang` | `[1..1]` | `string` | Two-letter Alpha-2 language code according to ISO 639. |
| `content` | `[1..1]` | `string` | Localized text value. |

> **Where it appears:** `MultiLangString` structures both `srvDescription` and `IntendedUse.purpose`, so multilingual display is a built-in part of the model rather than a presentation-layer afterthought.

**Class `IntendedUse` (`B.2.7`)**

| Attribute | Mult. | Type | RP-facing meaning |
|:----------|:-----:|:-----|:------------------|
| `purpose` | `[1..*]` | `MultiLangString` | One or more localized statements of the purpose of data processing. |
| `privacyPolicy` | `[1..*]` | `Policy` | Privacy-policy reference(s) associated with this intended use. |
| `createdAt` | `[1..1]` | `string` | Validity start date in `YYYY-MM-DD` format. |
| `revokedAt` | `[0..1]` | `string` | End date for the intended use if it is no longer valid. |
| `credential` | `[1..*]` | `Credential` | Requestable attestation/credential definitions for this intended use. |
| `intendedUseIdentifier` | `[1..1]` | `string` | Registrar-provided unique intended-use identifier. |

> **Layering note:** ETSI TS 119 475 Annex B contains an internal tension: its prose calls `intendedUseIdentifier` optional/reserved while the class table gives `[1..1]`. ARF v3 resolves the integration model at a higher layer: the Registrar creates intended-use identifiers, maps intended uses to Services, and issuance produces one certificate per pair. Implementations should follow the applicable ARF/profile extension for the wire member rather than treating the base-ETSI prose as permission to collapse intended uses.

**Class `Policy` (`B.2.8`)**

| Attribute | Mult. | Type | RP-facing meaning |
|:----------|:-----:|:-----|:------------------|
| `type` | `[1..1]` | `string` | URI identifying the policy type. In WRP attribute context, ETSI TS 119 475 defines only the privacy-policy URI type. |
| `policyURI` | `[1..1]` | `string` | URL where the policy is published. |

**Class `Credential` (`B.2.9`)**

| Attribute | Mult. | Type | RP-facing meaning |
|:----------|:-----:|:-----|:------------------|
| `format` | `[1..1]` | `string` | Credential/attestation format. |
| `meta` | `[1..1]` | `string` | Format-specific metadata or properties used to identify the credential type. |
| `claim` | `[0..*]` | `Claim` | Claim set that can be requested or issued. If absent, the WRP is not declaring specific attributes at this level. |

**Class `Claim` (`B.2.10`)**

| Attribute | Mult. | Type | RP-facing meaning |
|:----------|:-----:|:-----|:------------------|
| `path` | `[1..1]` | `string` | Path pointer identifying the claim within the credential structure. |
| `values` | `[0..1]` | `string` | Optional expected-value constraint set for the claim. ETSI TS 119 475 describes this as an array of strings, integers, or booleans even though the type column is rendered as `string`. |

**Class `Law` (`B.2.11`)**

| Attribute | Mult. | Type | RP-facing meaning |
|:----------|:-----:|:-----|:------------------|
| `lang` | `[1..1]` | `string` | Two-letter Alpha-2 language code according to ISO 639. |
| `legalBasis` | `[1..1]` | `string` | Legal basis under which the legal person is established, or under which access to a specific claim is required or recommended. |

> **Scope note:** ETSI TS 119 475 says `Law` is only used in the context of `LegalPerson`, so it is not a general-purpose free-standing claim-justification object across the whole model.

Taken together, Annex B gives a more precise RP-centric picture than the earlier TS5/TS6 summary alone: it separates support from informational contact channels, treats multilingual service descriptions and purposes as structured data, models intended-use lifecycle explicitly, and carries intermediary/public-body/provider semantics in a way that later maps directly into WRPRC payloads.

#### 4.3 Registration Process Overview

Each Member State must publish one or more national registration policies (CIR 2025/848 Art. 4). These policies must include at minimum the following 7 content items (Art. 4(3)):

| Item | Art. 4(3) | Content |
|:-----|:----------|:--------|
| 1 | (a) | Identification and authentication procedures for RPs during registration |
| 2 | (b) | Required supporting documentation (identity, business registration, entitlements) |
| 3 | (c) | Authentic sources or official electronic records relied upon for data accuracy |
| 4 | (d) | Any other information or evidence required as part of the process |
| 5 | (e) | Automated means for RPs to register or update an existing registration (where applicable) |
| 6 | **(f)** | **Redress mechanism** available to RPs under MS law — i.e., what recourse an RP has if registration is rejected or suspended |
| 7 | (g) | Rules and procedures for verifying the RP's identity and other relevant information |

> **RP relevance**: Item (f) — the redress mechanism — is particularly important. If an RP's registration is rejected or suspended (§4.3.2), the MS registration policy must specify how the RP can appeal or seek administrative review. RPs preparing for registration should consult their MS's published policy to understand the available remedies.

##### 4.3.1 Registration Sequence Diagram (Direct RP Model)

```mermaid
---
config:
  themeVariables:
    noteBkgColor: "transparent"
    noteBorderColor: "transparent"
  sequence:
    messageAlign: left
    noteAlign: left
    actorMargin: 250
---
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant RP as 🏦 Relying Party
    participant REG as 🏛️ Registrar<br/>(Member State)
    participant ACA as 🔐 Access CA

    REG->>REG: Validate application

    Note right of RP: RP data published in national register
    Note right of RCP: ⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀

    Note right of RCP: ⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
    end

    end
```

<details>
<summary><strong>1. Relying Party submits registration application to Registrar</strong></summary>

The Relying Party submits a registration application to the Registrar in its Member State. This submission formalizes its Services and the data each intended use will request. The exact authenticated submission flow is still Member State-specific, and TS5 leaves full `POST /wrp` harmonization for further study. The example therefore shows the required ARF v3 logical structure; a national API may use different field names while preserving the same Service boundaries and cardinalities. The RP supplies the Service identifiers, but the Registrar adds intended-use identifiers only after registration.

**Failure Path:** If the submitted data model fails schema validation, the Registrar returns a `400 Bad Request` and terminates the flow.

**Audit Telemetry:** The Relying Party triggers a `REGISTRATION_SUBMISSION_INITIATED` SIEM event.

```json
{
  "country": "DE",
  "identifier": [

      "type": "http://data.europa.eu/eudi/id/EUID",
      "identifier": "5299001GCLKH6FPVJW75"
    }
  ],
  "legalPerson": {
    "legalName": ["Example Bank AG"]
  },
  "supportURI": ["https://support.example-bank.de/eudi-wallet"],

  ],
  "supervisoryAuthority": {
    "name": "Der Bundesbeauftragte fuer den Datenschutz und die Informationsfreiheit",

              "format": "dc+sd-jwt",

                {"path": ["credentialSubject", "given_name"]},

      ]
    },
    {

      ],

          ],

              "type": "privacy_policy"
            }
          ],
          "credentials": [

              "format": "dc+sd-jwt",
              "meta": "eu.europa.ec.eudi.sca.payment.1",

              ]

```

</details>
<details>
<summary><strong>2. Registrar validates application</strong></summary>

The national Registrar processes the application according to the amended evidence taxonomy in CIR 2025/848 Article 6. It must not present the entire record as one uniformly approved dataset.

The routine has four distinct parts:

1. **Verified identity and establishment data** — The Registrar verifies the accuracy, validity, authenticity, and integrity of Annex I points `1–6`, including official name, identifiers, address, URL, and identifier-country syntax, against supporting documentation, authentic sources, or official electronic records.
2. **Verified status and relationship data** — The same verification standard applies to points `11–16`: public-body status, entitlements/sub-entitlements, intermediary use, and both directions of an intermediary association.
3. **Transparency-only automated collection** — Contact data, Service descriptions, requested data, and intended-use descriptions in points `7–10` are collected automatically. The Registrar does **not** preauthorise those fields. In particular, recording a claim and purpose does not mean the Registrar approved its GDPR legal basis, necessity, or proportionality.
4. **Structural registration processing** — The Registrar checks Service-identifier uniqueness within the RP, maps each intended use to one Service, assigns the EU-wide RP and intended-use identifiers, and prepares the exact `(Service, intended use)` records needed for certificate issuance.

**Failure Path:** Invalid verified evidence, an unverified entitlement/association, or a structurally invalid Service mapping prevents activation. Transparency-only data can fail schema or completeness checks, but it must not be rejected under an invented preauthorisation assessment.

**Audit Telemetry:** The Registrar generates a `REG_APP_VALIDATION_FAILED` SIEM event upon detecting anomalous or non-compliant registration data.

```json
{
  "validation_status": "IN_PROGRESS",
  "checks": [
    {"annex_points": "1-6", "class": "REGISTRAR_VERIFIED", "status": "VERIFIED"},
    {"annex_points": "11-16", "class": "REGISTRAR_VERIFIED", "status": "VERIFIED"},
    {"annex_points": "7-10", "class": "TRANSPARENCY_NO_PREAUTHORISATION", "status": "COLLECTED"},
    {"type": "SERVICE_INTENDED_USE_MAPPING", "status": "STRUCTURALLY_VALID"}
  ],
  "timestamp": "2026-06-15T09:30:00Z"
}
```

</details>
<details>
<summary><strong>3. Registrar confirms registration to Relying Party</strong></summary>

Upon successful processing, the Registrar commits the record to the authoritative national register, assigns the EU-wide RP identifier and intended-use identifiers, and preserves the evidence class of every field. The signed query surface described in `§4.4` publishes that record; it must not relabel transparency-only points `7–10` as Registrar-approved data.

This activation marks the Relying Party as active (`status: ACTIVE`), and the Registrar exposes the verified data via the public Registrar REST API (`GET /wrp/{identifier}`). This endpoint acts as the authoritative source, enabling:

- **Wallet Users, auditors, and public consumers**: To inspect published registration state outside the normal certificate-carrying presentation path.
- **Access CAs**: To verify active registration and obtain the RP, Service, intermediary-association, and national-register data required for each WRPAC (Step 5).
- **Registration Certificate CAs**: To retrieve the authoritative Service/intended-use record required for each WRPRC (Steps 10–12).
- **Supervisory Authorities**: To continuously monitor, audit, and regulate active Relying Parties.

**Failure Path:** If the Relying Party later violates ecosystem rules or GDPR mandates, the Registrar updates the authoritative register state and triggers the downstream suspension/cancellation and certificate-revocation cascade described in `§4.3.2`.

**Artifact Produced:** Authoritative register entry and `registryURI`.

**Audit Telemetry:** The Registrar logs `REGISTRATION_ACTIVATED` and propagates state changes to national notification services.

```http
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
Location: https://api.registrar.de/wrp/5299001GCLKH6FPVJW75

# Member State-specific acknowledgement body omitted intentionally:
# TS5 leaves POST response harmonisation for further study.
# The interoperable follow-up surface is the signed GET response on /wrp or /wrp/{identifier}.
```

> **Record Retention (Art. 10):** Registrars retain records of all Relying Party registration information—including all subsequent changes—for **10 years** (CIR 2025/848 Art. 10). This retention serves *ex post* monitoring, law enforcement investigations, and dispute handling. Relying Parties must ensure their entire registration history remains auditable.

</details>
<details>
<summary><strong>4. Relying Party requests WRPAC(s) from Access CA</strong></summary>

With a confirmed registration, the RP obtains a WRPAC for every RP Instance/Service binding it will deploy. The RP Instance generates a secure key pair within its infrastructure, for example in an HSM or secure enclave, and returns only the public-key/CSR material to the RP.

The RP sends the CSR to the Access CA together with the Registrar-assigned RP identifier and RP-chosen Service identifier. The CA validates those identifiers against the register and issues under ETSI TS 119 411-8 V1.1.1. The resulting certificate, rather than the CSR alone, binds the Instance public key to the RP and Service identifiers/trade names, applicable intermediary association, and national-register reference required by the amended profile.

**Failure Path:** If the CSR is malformed or uses an unsupported signature algorithm, the Access CA rejects the request and returns a `400 Bad Request`.

**Artifact Produced:** Cryptographic Key Pair (Private Key secured in HSM/KMS).

**Audit Telemetry:** The Relying Party logs a `WRPAC_CSR_GENERATED` SIEM event.

```text
Certificate Request:
    Data:
        Version: 1 (0x0)
        Subject: C=DE, O=Example Bank AG, serialNumber=5299001GCLKH6FPVJW75, CN=onboarding.example-bank.de
        Subject Public Key Info:
            Public Key Algorithm: id-ecPublicKey
                Public-Key: (256 bit)
                pub:
                    04:a1:b2:c3:d4... [EC Public Key]
        Attributes:
            Requested Extensions:
                X509v3 Subject Alternative Name:
                    DNS:onboarding.example-bank.de
    Signature Algorithm: ecdsa-with-SHA256
         30:45:02:20:7c... [Signature]
```

> **One WRPAC per Instance/Service binding:** Each independent component needs Service-appropriate certificate material. If one backend serves both `bank-onboarding` and `payment-approval`, it receives two WRPACs even if both certificates bind the same Instance public key. The RP must prevent one Service from selecting the other's certificate; protocol-specific `client_id` checks are additional to, not a substitute for, the RP/Service identifier match.

</details>
<details>
<summary><strong>5. Access CA queries Registrar to verify Relying Party registration</strong></summary>

The Access Certificate Authority (Access CA) operates under defined issuance policies and validates certificate requests using national registries. Upon receiving the CSR, the Access CA serves as a verification control point by querying the designated Registrar REST API (`GET /wrp/{identifier}`).

This verification step connects the PKI trust layer and the national registration layer. The Access CA validates four mandatory conditions:
1. **Existence & Status**: The Relying Party must exist in the national registry and hold an `ACTIVE` status.
2. **Identifier Matching**: The registered RP identifier carried in the CSR subject data (for example an EUID or Member State-specific unique identifier) must match the identifier registered with the authority.
3. **Service Matching**: The requested Service identifier and Service trade name must belong to that RP, and the intended certificate must correspond to the RP Instance/Service binding being enrolled.
4. **Standing**: The Relying Party and Service must not be suspended, cancelled, or otherwise ineligible for issuance.

```http
GET /wrp/5299001GCLKH6FPVJW75 HTTP/1.1
Host: api.registrar.de
Authorization: Bearer [Access_CA_Privileged_Token]
Accept: application/jwt
```

**Failure Path:** If any condition fails, the Access CA immediately aborts the issuance process and logs the denied request. This safeguard helps ensure that unregistered, suspended, or unauthorized entities cannot obtain the cryptographic WRPACs necessary to interface with EUDI Wallet Units.

**Audit Telemetry:** The Access CA generates a `CA_REG_LOOKUP_DENIED` SIEM alert.

> **CA-Registrar binding**: This verification step is what connects the PKI trust layer (X.509 certificates) to the regulatory trust layer (national registration). A WRPAC without a backing Registrar entry is invalid by design.

</details>
<details>
<summary><strong>6. Registrar confirms registration to Access CA</strong></summary>

The Registrar responds to the same `/wrp/{identifier}` API call by returning the Relying Party's registered data points as a JWS-signed payload. In practice, the Access CA treats that signed register view as the authoritative confirmation that the RP is currently active and eligible for certificate issuance under the applicable national policy.

**Artifact Produced:** Registration Data Payload (JWS).

**Audit Telemetry:** The Access CA logs `REGISTRATION_CONFIRMED_BY_REGISTRAR`.

```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/jwt
x-jku-url: https://api.registrar.de/.well-known/jwks.json

eyJhbGciOiJFUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCIsImtpZCI6InJlZ2lzdHJhci0xIn0.
{
  "iss": "urn:eudi:registrar:de:bafin",
  "iat": 1718445123,
  "data": {
    "identifier": [
      {
        "type": "http://data.europa.eu/eudi/id/EUID",
        "identifier": "5299001GCLKH6FPVJW75"
      }
    ],
    "country": "DE",
    "legalPerson": {
      "legalName": ["Example Bank AG"]
    },
    "tradeName": "Example Bank",
    "serviceIdentifier": "bank-onboarding",
    "serviceTradeName": "Example Bank Onboarding",
    "registryURI": "https://api.registrar.de/wrp/5299001GCLKH6FPVJW75",
    "entitlements": [
      "https://uri.etsi.org/19475/Entitlement/Service_Provider"
    ]
  }
}.
[signature_bytes]
```

</details>
<details>
<summary><strong>7. Access CA issues X.509 Access Certificate</strong></summary>

The Access CA mints the X.509 WRPAC under ETSI TS 119 411-8 V1.1.1. The certificate binds the RP Instance public key to the EU-wide RP identifier and trade name, the applicable Service identifier and Service trade name, and a reference to the national register. If the subject is an intermediary, the certificate also carries the associated end-RP identifier and end-RP Service identifier. ETSI TS 119 475 remains relevant to cross-certificate data consistency, but it is not the WRPAC certificate-policy profile.

**Artifact Produced:** The X.509 Wallet Relying Party Access Certificate (WRPAC).

**Audit Telemetry:** The Access CA logs a `WRPAC_CERT_ISSUED` SIEM event.

```text
Certificate:
    Data:
        Version: 3 (0x2)
        Serial Number: 1234567890 (0x499602d2)
        Issuer: C=DE, O=Access CA GMBH, CN=EUDI WRPAC CA 1
        Subject: C=DE, O=Example Bank AG, serialNumber=5299001GCLKH6FPVJW75, CN=Example Bank EUDI Web Service
        X509v3 extensions:
            X509v3 Subject Alternative Name:
                DNS:onboarding.example-bank.de
            EUDI RP Service Identifier: bank-onboarding
            EUDI RP Service Trade Name: Example Bank Onboarding
            National Register Reference:
                URI:https://api.registrar.de/wrp/5299001GCLKH6FPVJW75
```

</details>
<details>
<summary><strong>8. Access CA delivers WRPAC to Relying Party</strong></summary>

The Access CA delivers the WRPAC together with its signing certificate and any intermediate certificate(s) leading up to—but not substituting for—the Access CA trust anchor in the Commission-published LoTE. The RP must retain that delivered chain as one inventory unit; the Wallet obtains the trust anchor through the LoTE rather than trusting a root supplied by the RP.

The Relying Party must immediately secure the corresponding private key within a resilient, hardware-backed key store (e.g., an HSM or managed Cloud KMS) to prevent key exfiltration. This private cryptographic material acts as the ultimate anchor for the Relying Party's authenticity, and is utilized across two primarily integration vectors:

- **Online Authentication**: To securely sign JSON-Secured Authorization Requests (JARs). The entire WRPAC chain is injected into the `x5c` header of the JWS payload, allowing remote Wallet Units to verify the signature.
- **Proximity Authentication**: To sign `readerAuth` structures during offline BLE/NFC mdoc presentations. The WRPAC is embedded directly in the COSE_Sign1 unprotected header.

```json
{
  "alg": "ES256",
  "typ": "oauth-authz-req+jwt",
  "x5c": [
    "MIIB... (WRPAC Leaf)",
    "MIIB... (Access CA Signing / Intermediate)"
  ]
}
```

Because WRPACs carry high systemic risk if compromised, they possess a strictly limited validity period (typically 1–2 years). Relying Parties must engineer automated cryptographic rotation pipelines to renew WRPACs prior to expiration, as Wallet Units forcefully reject expired certificates at runtime.

</details>
<details>
<summary><strong>9. Access CA logs WRPAC to Certificate Transparency</strong></summary>

Where an access-certificate CT log is available, ARF Topic 55 turns Certificate Transparency from a future watchlist item into a concrete access-certificate profile. The Access CA submits the newly minted WRPAC or corresponding precertificate to an RFC 9162 CT log and obtains a cryptographic Signed Certificate Timestamp (SCT), which is a commitment that the entry will be merged into the append-only log within the declared Maximum Merge Delay (MMD); inclusion and consistency proofs remain separate evidence surfaces.

This architectural requirement aligns the EUDI PKI with modern Web PKI standards and provides three critical security properties:

1. **Ecosystem-wide Auditability**: CT logs give monitors, auditors, Wallet operators, and RPs a shared visibility surface for detecting rogue, mis-issued, or compromised WRPACs.
2. **Additional Transparency**: Public logging creates an auditable issuance trail tying the Access CA, the RP identity, and the transparency evidence together, making unauthorized issuance easier to investigate.
3. **Wallet-side SCT validation**: Topic 55 requires an Access CA to include at least one SCT in each access certificate and requires the Wallet Unit to verify at least one valid SCT during issuance or presentation. If the access certificate lacks a valid SCT in that profile, the Wallet handles it as an RP-authentication failure under `RPA_06a`.

**Failure Path:** If no CT log is available for access certificates, `CT_01` keeps logging conditional. If the CT profile applies and the WRPAC does not carry a valid SCT, the Wallet-side result is an RP-authentication failure. Temporary log outage, MMD delay, delayed inclusion evidence, and rogue issuance remain different operational states; CT evidence does not replace certificate revocation or Registrar/Access CA suspension action.

**Artifact Produced:** Signed Certificate Timestamp (SCT).

**Audit Telemetry:** The Access CA logs a `WRPAC_CT_LOGGED` SIEM event.

```text
Certificate Extensions:
    CT Precertificate SCTs:
        Signed Certificate Timestamp:
            Version   : v1 (0x0)
            Log ID    : 5c:a1:... (EUDI Public Log)
            Timestamp : Jun 15 14:26:00 2026 GMT
            Extensions: none
            Signature : ecdsa-with-SHA256
                        30:45:02:20:12...
```

> **Scope boundary**: Topic 55 settles the SCT-presence failure semantics for the access-certificate profile, but it does not settle EU CT log admission, lifecycle governance, monitor/auditor operations, or inclusion-proof expectations. CT is the transparency layer, not the revocation authority.

</details>
<details>
<summary><strong>10. Registrar triggers automated issuance for every Service/intended-use pair</strong></summary>

After activation, the Registrar initiates WRPRC issuance for every registered `(Service, intended use)` pair. CIR 2026/1730 requires the authorized Registration Certificate CA to issue automatically and without undue delay; the RP is not expected to make an optional one-certificate request after onboarding.

For the two-Service example in Step 1, the Registrar emits one issuance job for `bank-onboarding/KYC` and one for `payment-approval/SCA`. Each job carries the exact identifiers needed to prevent a flat RP-wide certificate from authorizing both Services.

**Artifact Produced:** Register-controlled certificate-issuance job.

**Audit Telemetry:** The Registrar logs `WRPRC_AUTOMATED_ISSUANCE_TRIGGERED` once per Service/intended-use pair.

```json
{
  "rpIdentifier": "5299001GCLKH6FPVJW75",
  "serviceIdentifier": "bank-onboarding",
  "intendedUseIdentifier": "urn:eudi:wrp:de:bank-example:kyc",
  "registrationRecordVersion": "2026-12-24T09:30:00Z"
}
```

</details>
<details>
<summary><strong>11. Registration Certificate CA retrieves the authoritative Service/intended-use record</strong></summary>

To construct the WRPRC accurately, the Registration Certificate CA sources the current authoritative record for the exact pair identified by the issuance job. Under ETSI TS 119 475 V1.2.1, it verifies that the RP is listed, that the certificate contents match the register, and that the RP holds at least one valid WRPAC with the same RP and Service identifiers/trade names.

The backend interface is national; the following request is illustrative rather than a harmonized Wallet-facing API:

```http
GET /wrp/5299001GCLKH6FPVJW75?serviceIdentifier=bank-onboarding
    &intendedUseIdentifier=urn%3Aeudi%3Awrp%3Ade%3Abank-example%3Akyc HTTP/1.1
Host: api.registrar.de
Accept: application/jwt
Authorization: Bearer [RCP_Privileged_Token]
```

This backend-to-backend integration guarantees that the WRPRC is minted from current register state rather than stale RP-supplied inputs. The CA may rely on Registrar-side identity proofing under the national policy instead of repeating a full proofing cycle for every Service/use certificate.

**Failure Path:** If the Relying Party's registration is suspended or not found, the Registrar returns a `404 Not Found` or `403 Forbidden`, and the Provider aborts issuance.

**Audit Telemetry:** The Provider generates a `RCP_REG_LOOKUP_DENIED` SIEM alert if the lookup is unsuccessful.

</details>
<details>
<summary><strong>12. Registrar returns registration data to Registration Cert Provider</strong></summary>

The Registrar returns a signed record for exactly one Service/intended-use pair. The CA maps RP and Service trade names/identifiers, the single intended use, general access policy, requested credential/claim scope, and supporting transparency/status data into the ETSI TS 119 475 V1.2.1 payload. It must not merge other Services or intended uses into that certificate.

**Artifact Produced:** Registration Data Payload (JWS).

**Audit Telemetry:** The Registrar logs `REGISTRATION_DATA_SERVED_TO_RCP`.

<details>
<summary><strong>13. Registration Cert Provider issues WRPRC</strong></summary>

The Registration Certificate CA mints one WRPRC under ETSI TS 119 475 V1.2.1, supplemented by the ARF v3 requirement that the format carry the applicable Service identifier and Service trade name. The artifact uses JWT or CWT, AdES B-B signature handling, the ETSI payload model, and lifecycle/status fields. Its general access policy tells the Wallet that the RP may request only the data specified for the certificate's single intended use.

For a service-provider example, that means the certificate carries:

- Base transparency fields such as `name`, `sub`, `country`, `registry_uri`, `srv_description`, `entitlements`, `privacy_policy`, `info_uri`, `support_uri`, `supervisory_authority`, `policy_id`, `certificate_policy`, and `iat`
- The profile-defined Service identifier and Service trade name, matching one or more WRPACs for the same RP Service
- Service-provider authorization fields such as `credentials`, `purpose`, and `intended_use_id`
- The harmonized general access policy required by amended CIR 2025/848 Article 8(2)(c)
- Lifecycle/status fields such as `exp`, `id`, and the status-list reference used for later validity checks

**Artifact Produced:** The Wallet Relying Party Registration Certificate (WRPRC JWT).

**Audit Telemetry:** The Provider logs `WRPRC_ISSUED`.

```json
{
  "alg": "ES256",
  "typ": "rc-wrp+jwt",
  "x5c": [
    "...provider leaf...",
    "...provider intermediate..."
  ]
}
```
