| **Issuer** | PID Provider (notified per MS) | LPID Provider (national business register) |
| **Authentic source** | Civil registries, population registers | Business registers (BRIS-connected) |
| **mdoc profile** | `eu.europa.ec.eudi.pid.1` (standardised) | Not yet standardised — SD-JWT VC only |

#### 20.4 EBW Legislative Status and RP Readiness

| Date / status | Milestone |
|:--------------|:----------|
| 19 Nov 2025 | Commission published COM(2025) 838 and opened procedure `2025/0358(COD)` |
| 18 Mar 2026 | European Economic and Social Committee adopted its opinion on the proposal |
| 26 Jul 2026 | EUR-Lex records the ordinary legislative procedure as **ongoing**; no final adoption, entry-into-force, or deployment date should be inferred |

| Priority | Action | When |
|:---------|:-------|:-----|
| 🔴 **Now** | Design attestation processing pipelines to be entity-type-agnostic — do not hardcode natural person PID attributes | Immediately |
| 🔴 **Now** | Ensure DCQL query construction can handle multiple `vct_values` and multi-credential requests | Immediately |
| 🟡 **Source watch** | Map the final EBW law, implementing acts, trust lists, relying-party authentication, registration, credential types, and transition dates | When each authoritative source is published |
| 🟡 **Profile gate** | Add EUID and LPID validation under a versioned governing profile; keep EWC pilot types isolated from production allowlists | When the selected LPID profile is authoritative for the deployment |
| 🟢 **Rulebook gate** | Activate mandate-scope verification for each supported representation Rulebook and vocabulary | When a Rulebook is discoverable and accepted by policy |
| 🟢 **Deployment gate** | Enable LPID + PID + mandate combinations only after compatible wallets, issuers, trust sources, and test evidence exist | Per deployment, not by forecast year |

#### 20.5 LPID Credential Format and Profile Gaps

The Legal Person Identification Data (LPID) attestation uses the same `dc+sd-jwt` format profile as the natural person PID (§6.1). The LPID attribute model is defined above; this subsection covers the credential format specifics relevant to RP verification pipelines.

##### 20.5.1 VCT Value and Issuer Metadata

EWC RFC005 §6.10.4 defines the LPID attestation with VCT value `EWC_LPID_Attestation`. The credential issuer metadata entry:

```json
{
  "credential_configurations_supported": {
    "EWC_LPID_Attestation": {
      "format": "dc+sd-jwt",
      "vct": "EWC_LPID_Attestation",
      "claims": {
        "legal_person_id": {
          "display": [{"name": "The EUID of the company", "locale": "en-GB"}]
        },
        "legal_person_name": {
          "display": [{"name": "The name of the company", "locale": "en-GB"}]
        },
        "issuer_name": {
          "display": [{"name": "Name of issuer from the MS that issued the ODI instance", "locale": "en-GB"}]
        },
        "issuer_id": {
          "display": [{"name": "Id of the issuing authority (Business register identifier for BRIS)", "locale": "en-GB"}]
        },
        "issuer_country": {
          "display": [{"name": "Alpha-2 country code of the issuing country", "locale": "en-GB"}]
        },
        "issuance_date": {
          "display": [{"name": "Date and possibly time of issuance", "locale": "en-GB"}]
        },
        "expiry_date": {
          "display": [{"name": "Date and possibly time of expiration", "locale": "en-GB"}]
        },
        "authentic_source_id": {
          "display": [{"name": "Source of the issuing (Business register identifier for BRIS)", "locale": "en-GB"}]
        },
        "authentic_source_name": {
          "display": [{"name": "Name of issuer from the MS that issued the instance", "locale": "en-GB"}]
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Key observations for RPs:
- **VCT value**: `EWC_LPID_Attestation` — distinct from `eu.europa.ec.eudi.pid.1`. RPs must check the `vct` claim to distinguish natural person from legal person credentials.
- **Format**: `dc+sd-jwt` — identical format profile to natural person PID. The same SD-JWT VC verification pipeline applies (§13.3).
- **Selective disclosure**: All claims are independently disclosable via SD-JWT's `_sd` mechanism.
- **Key binding**: The EWC SD-JWT VC example uses the ordinary `cnf`/KB-JWT holder-binding model. That verifies the LPID credential's own bound key; it does not require an LPID, PID, and mandate to reuse one `cnf.jwk`.

> **VCT standardisation gap**: The VCT value `EWC_LPID_Attestation` is defined by the EWC consortium (RFC005). The ARF does not yet define an official LPID VCT. A future standardised value (potentially `eu.europa.ec.eudi.lpid.1`, following the naming convention of the natural person PID) may supersede the EWC value. RPs should implement VCT matching using a configurable allowlist rather than hardcoded string comparison.

##### 20.5.2 JSON Schema

EWC RFC005 clause 6.10.3 provides the JSON Schema for LPID credential subject validation. The `credential_subject` object requires exactly two fields:

```json
{
  "credential_subject": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "legal_person_id": {
        "description": "Unique id for organisations in EUID structure.",
        "type": "string"
      },
      "legal_person_name": {
        "description": "Official current legal person name as registered in the business register.",
        "type": "string"
      }
    },
    "required": ["legal_person_id", "legal_person_name"]
  }
}
```

##### 20.5.3 mdoc Format Gap

RFC005 does not define an mdoc profile for LPID. The EWC specification focuses exclusively on SD-JWT VC. For EUDI ecosystem proximity use cases, an mdoc encoding would likely use `docType` value `eu.europa.ec.eudi.lpid.1` (analogous to `eu.europa.ec.eudi.pid.1`), but this is not standardised.

> **Specification gap**: The absence of an mdoc LPID profile means proximity-based LPID presentation is not currently standardised. RPs expecting proximity-based legal person verification should plan for SD-JWT VC over remote flows or await mdoc LPID standardisation.

#### 20.6 Legal-Person Request Patterns

When an RP interacts with a legal person — e.g., for B2B onboarding, procurement, or contract signing — it uses LPID-specific DCQL queries. The core pattern is to request only the organisation evidence needed for the decision, then add representative PID and mandate credentials only when authority must be proven.

##### 20.6.1 LPID-Only: Simple Company Verification

For use cases requiring only company identity (e.g., VAT verification, procurement eligibility check):

```json
{
  "credentials": [
    {
      "id": "lpid",
      "format": "dc+sd-jwt",
      "meta": { "vct_values": ["EWC_LPID_Attestation"] },
      "claims": [
        {"path": ["legal_person_id"]},
        {"path": ["legal_person_name"]}
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

##### 20.6.2 LPID and Natural Person PID: Representative Identification

For use cases where the RP must identify both the company and the person interacting on its behalf:

```json
{
  "credentials": [
    {
      "id": "lpid",
      "format": "dc+sd-jwt",
      "meta": { "vct_values": ["EWC_LPID_Attestation"] },
      "claims": [
        {"path": ["legal_person_id"]},
        {"path": ["legal_person_name"]}
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "pid",
      "format": "dc+sd-jwt",
      "meta": { "vct_values": ["urn:eudi:pid:1"] },
      "claims": [
        {"path": ["family_name"]},
        {"path": ["given_name"]},
        {"path": ["birthdate"]}
      ]
    }
  ],
  "credential_sets": [
    {
      "purpose": "Identify company and its representative",
      "options": [["lpid", "pid"]]
    }
  ]
}
```

##### 20.6.3 LPID and PID and Mandate: Triple-Credential Corporate Onboarding

For high-assurance B2B use cases (financial onboarding, contract signing authority) where the RP must verify the company identity, the representative's personal identity, **and** their authority to act on behalf of the company:

```json
{
  "credentials": [
    {
      "id": "company_id",
      "format": "dc+sd-jwt",
      "meta": { "vct_values": ["EWC_LPID_Attestation"] },
      "claims": [
        {"path": ["legal_person_id"]},
        {"path": ["legal_person_name"]}
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "representative_pid",
      "format": "dc+sd-jwt",
      "meta": { "vct_values": ["urn:eudi:pid:1"] },
      "claims": [
        {"path": ["family_name"]},
        {"path": ["given_name"]},
        {"path": ["birthdate"]},
        {"path": ["personal_administrative_number"]}
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "mandate",
      "format": "dc+sd-jwt",
      "meta": { "vct_values": ["eu.europa.ec.eudi.mandate.1"] },
      "claims": [
        {"path": ["representation_type"]},
        {"path": ["representative_id"]},
        {"path": ["represented_entity_id"]},
        {"path": ["represented_entity_name"]},
        {"path": ["scope_of_authority"]},
        {"path": ["validity_period"]},
        {"path": ["corporate_role"]},
        {"path": ["joint_representation"]}
      ]
    }
  ],
  "credential_sets": [
    {
      "purpose": "Corporate client onboarding — verify company identity, representative identity, and authorisation to act",
      "options": [["company_id", "representative_pid", "mandate"]]
    }
  ]
}
```

> **Illustrative-only request**: The VCT and claim names above are architecture placeholders, not a production DCQL contract. No final ARF or EBW credential schema assigns `eu.europa.ec.eudi.mandate.1`. Current Annex Topic 29 (`RP_01`, `RP_02`) covers natural-person-to-natural-person representation Rulebooks. Directive (EU) 2025/25 defines a narrower digital EU power of attorney for specified cross-border company-law procedures, while COM(2025) 838 proposes EBW mandate and access-control functionality whose final technical profile remains unsettled. Bind production requests to an accepted, versioned Rulebook/profile.

**Joint Representation (Gesamtvertretung)**

Some corporate mandates require **joint exercise** — two or more representatives must act together for the mandate to be valid. This pattern, known as *Gesamtvertretung* in German corporate law, has no equivalent in natural-person-to-natural-person representation. The mandate credential signals this via two attributes:

- `joint_representation` (boolean) — `true` if this mandate requires joint exercise with another representative
- `joint_partner_ids` (array) — identifiers of the other required representatives

When the RP receives a mandate with `joint_representation: true`, it must collect valid mandates from ALL listed joint partners before authorising the operation. This may require:

1. **Multi-session orchestration** — the RP initiates separate OpenID4VP sessions with each joint representative's Wallet, then binds the results into a single authorisation decision
2. **Temporal binding** — all joint mandates must be valid at the same point in time (not sequentially revoked-and-reissued)
3. **Scope intersection** — the effective scope is the intersection of all joint mandates' `scope_of_authority`

> **Planning pattern, not protocol semantics**: No current ARF, OID4VP, Topic 29, Directive (EU) 2025/25, or final EBW profile assigns the illustrative `joint_representation` fields or a multi-Wallet ceremony. If the governing company-law source and credential profile require joint action, orchestrate it at application level and preserve each representative's separately verified evidence; do not advertise the illustrative field names as interoperable.

##### 20.6.4 Mandate-Only DCQL Query

For use cases where the RP already knows the company (e.g., an existing customer portal) and only needs to verify the representative's authority:

```json
{
  "credentials": [
    {
      "id": "mandate",
      "format": "dc+sd-jwt",
      "meta": { "vct_values": ["eu.europa.ec.eudi.mandate.1"] },
      "claims": [
        {"path": ["representation_type"]},
        {"path": ["representative_id"]},
        {"path": ["represented_entity_id"]},
        {"path": ["scope_of_authority"]}
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

> **Illustrative-only request and assurance trade-off**: The VCT and fields are placeholders until a governing profile defines them. A mandate-only presentation can authenticate its own bound presenter only to the extent specified by that profile; without co-presented PID/LPID, the RP must use separately current identity/entity evidence and the Rulebook's subject-binding rules. Do not infer that mandate signature validity alone establishes the representative's natural-person identity or the represented entity's current status.

#### 20.7 Cross-Entity Binding and Verification Delta

When an RP receives a combined presentation involving LPID, PID, and potentially a mandate credential, it must perform **three relationship decisions**:

1. **Presenter/holder evidence**: Verify each credential's own holder binding. If a Topic 18 common-management proof is profiled, it may bind distinct keys under one WSCA/WSCD or keystore boundary. Do not require one `cnf.jwk` across LPID, PID, and mandate credentials.
2. **Representative ↔ PID binding** (attribute-based): the mandate representative identifier matches the representative PID subject identifier under the applicable Rulebook or credential profile — proving the natural person presenting is the authorised representative.
3. **Mandate ↔ LPID binding** (attribute-based): `mandate.represented_entity_id` == `lpid.legal_person_id` — proving the mandate applies to the presented legal person.

> **Key difference from natural-person combined presentations**: Natural person combined presentations (§19.1) only need to verify same-User binding — one entity, multiple credentials. LPID combined presentations require **cross-entity binding** — proving that Person A is authorised to act for Company B. This is structurally more complex, requiring attribute-level cross-matching in addition to the standard cryptographic or presentation-based binding described in §19.4.

The three-way binding check is performed after individual credential verification (§13.3 for SD-JWT VC) and before the RP's business logic processes the verified claims. If any binding check fails, the entire combined presentation must be rejected.

| Pipeline Step | Natural Person PID | LPID | Delta |
|:-------------|:------------------|:-----|:------|
| **1. Signature verification** | ECDSA P-256 / EdDSA over SD-JWT | Same | None |
| **2. Issuer trust** | Verify against the authorized PID Provider trust source | Resolve the authorized LPID/owner-identification provider under the governing pilot or final EBW profile | **New, profile-gated trust source** |
| **3. Key binding** | Verify `cnf.jwk` matches device key proof | Same mechanism | None |
| **4. Status/revocation check** | Applicable EUDI PID mechanism | Apply the LPID/owner-identification profile's selected mechanism and authorized signer | **Do not assume Topic 7 mechanism parity** |
| **5. Attribute validation** | `family_name`, `given_name`, `birth_date`, etc. | `legal_person_id`, `legal_person_name` — validate EUID format | **New validation rules** |
| **6. Cross-credential binding** | Same-User evidence at the required assurance; credential keys may differ | Presenter/representative/entity relationship checks under the mandate and LPID profiles | **Additional subject and authority checks** |
| **7. Scope verification** | Not applicable | Verify mandate `scope_of_authority` covers requested operation | **New step** |

##### 20.7.1 New Trust Anchor Set

The EWC pilot models business-register-oriented LPID Providers, while COM(2025) 838 proposes that Business Wallet owner identification data may be issued by qualified trust service providers, public sector bodies, or the Commission for Union entities. The final trust-list and certificate profiles are not established by the EUDI ARF. RPs should therefore:

1. **Create a separate provider-class resolver** for the accepted LPID or Business Wallet owner-identification profile rather than injecting pilot anchors into the PID Provider LoTE
2. **Validate the issuer and status authority** against the trust source authorized by that exact profile and source generation
3. **Keep pilot, proposal, and enacted-profile evidence distinct** in configuration and audit records

##### 20.7.2 EUID Format Validation

After verifying the LPID credential's signature and trust chain, the RP should validate the `legal_person_id` claim format (§20.3.1):

```
Pattern: &lt;CountryCode>&lt;BusinessRegisterCode>.&lt;DomesticRegistrationNumber>[_&lt;ValidationChar>]
Regex:   ^[A-Z]{2}[A-Z0-9]+\.[A-Z0-9]+(_[A-Z0-9])?$
```

A malformed EUID indicates a non-compliant LPID credential. The RP should reject or flag the presentation.

**Multi-subject binding caveat.** TR 119 479-1's role model matters for LPID, mandate, vehicle, product-passport, and other object or representation EAAs because one EAA can involve more than one subject. Wallet binding proves that the presenter controls a wallet-held key; it does not automatically prove that every subject or every attribute inside a multi-subject EAA belongs to the Wallet Holder. The RP should verify the binding at the level the Rulebook or EAA Policy defines: representative PID to mandate subject, `represented_entity_id` to LPID `legal_person_id`, object identifier to ownership/use entitlement, or certificate/signature context to the signing subject.

##### 20.7.3 Mandate Scope Verification

When a mandate or representation credential is presented alongside LPID and PID (§20.6.3), the RP must add a **scope verification** step: determine whether the asserted authorization covers the exact operation. Topic 29 `RP_01` permits each Attestation Scheme Provider to create one or more natural-to-natural representation Rulebooks. Every such Rulebook must specify a unique type and validity plus the nature of representation and authorized operations. It does not require the Commission to publish one universal Rulebook or vocabulary.

**Four Scope Enforcement Patterns**

RPs can implement scope checking using one of four patterns, ordered by implementation complexity:

| Pattern | Mechanism | Advantage | Disadvantage |
|:--------|:----------|:----------|:-------------|
| **1. String Matching** | `scope.operations CONTAINS rp_operation` — exact string comparison | Simple; no external vocabulary needed | Brittle — `"contract_signing"` ≠ `"sign_contract"`; no hierarchy; fragile across jurisdictions |
| **2. Structured JSON** ★ | Three sub-fields: `operations`, `limitations`, `exclusions` — RP evaluates all three | Handles constraints (amount caps, geographic scope); forward-compatible | Requires structured scope in credential; no cross-border vocabulary |
| **3. Vocabulary Hierarchies** | Rulebook-defined parent-child scope vocabulary — `financial_transactions` may imply `wire_transfer` only if that vocabulary says so | Enables controlled hierarchical resolution | Multiple scheme-provider Rulebooks can use incompatible terms and inheritance |
| **4. Policy-Based** | Mandate embeds/references a machine-readable policy (XACML, OPA/Rego) | Maximum flexibility | RP must implement policy evaluation engine; trust the policy source; handle versioning |

> **Recommendation**: Implement a schema-neutral adapter interface now, but activate a concrete parser only for an accepted, versioned Rulebook or EBW mandate profile. The Pattern 2 JSON below is a solved design example for an RP-controlled test profile, not a claim schema that wallets or issuers currently implement. A future Rulebook may choose strings, structured fields, a vocabulary, or a policy reference.

**Pattern 2 — Structured JSON Evaluation Algorithm**

This illustrative RP-controlled test profile uses three sub-fields:

```json
{
  "operations": ["contract_signing", "financial_transactions"],
  "limitations": {
    "max_transaction_value": { "amount": 50000, "currency": "EUR" },
    "geographic_scope": "EU",
    "time_restriction": "business_hours"
  },
  "exclusions": ["share_transfer", "liquidation"]
}
```

The RP evaluates scope in three steps:

1. **Operation check**: Verify the RP's operation identifier is present in `operations` and NOT present in `exclusions`
2. **Limitation check**: For each applicable limitation:
   - `max_transaction_value` → compare transaction value against ceiling
   - `geographic_scope` → verify RP's jurisdiction is within scope
   - `time_restriction` → verify current time falls within restriction
3. **Result**: PASS if the operation check succeeds AND all limitation checks pass; FAIL otherwise

**Ambiguity Handling**

When scope is ambiguous — the requested operation is not clearly covered or excluded — the RP must apply a configured ambiguity policy:

| Strategy | Description | When to Use |
|:---------|:------------|:------------|
| **Deny by default** | If the operation is not explicitly listed, reject | High-value operations (financial, contractual) |
| **Allow with logging** | Accept but log the ambiguity for audit review | Low-value operations (information access, status queries) |
| **Escalate** | Request a more specific mandate credential, or contact the represented entity directly | Available as fallback but should not be the default path |

> **RP guidance**: Never treat ambiguity as proof of authority. Deny or escalate whenever the operation requires established authorization. A low-risk service may offer a separate, non-authoritative path that does not rely on the mandate; it should not convert an ambiguous mandate into an allow decision merely because the event is logged.

**Pluggable Module Architecture**

The mandate scope verification step should be implemented as a **pluggable module** with a configurable scope vocabulary, enabling the RP to adapt as the specification landscape matures:

1. **Adapter phase (now)**: Define a versioned interface and fixtures without hard-coding illustrative claim names into the production credential parser
2. **Profile onboarding**: For each accepted scheme-provider Rulebook or EBW mandate profile, ingest its catalogue identity, schema, type identifier, vocabulary/version, trust/status sources, and semantic tests
3. **Interface**: The module should expose a simple `evaluateScope(mandate_scope, rp_operation, transaction_context) → { PASS | FAIL | AMBIGUOUS }` interface, allowing the RP's business logic to remain decoupled from scope evaluation internals

> **Governance gap**: Topic 29 allows multiple Attestation Scheme Providers and multiple Rulebooks. The unresolved RP questions are catalogue discovery, type collisions, schema/vocabulary versioning, coverage across schemes, semantic equivalence between jurisdictions, and which Rulebooks policy accepts. Natural-to-legal-person EBW mandates are a separate proposal/profile track; Directive (EU) 2025/25 already establishes a narrower digital EU power-of-attorney template for specified company-law procedures.

#### 20.8 Mandate and Representation Credentials

##### 20.8.1 Overview

The EUDI ecosystem defines **two fundamentally different representation paradigms** that share the label "mandate" but differ in legal basis, issuance authority, scope semantics, and revocation model:

```
Mandate Credentials
├── Paradigm A: Natural-to-Natural Representation
│   ├── Legal guardian for minor (Art. 3(1), Brussels IIb)
│   ├── Court-appointed guardian for incapacitated adult (Hague 2000)
│   └── Power of attorney for natural person (national civil law)
│
└── Paradigm B: Business-Wallet / Company Representation
    ├── Company director / board member (company register entry)
    ├── Employee with delegated signing authority (internal corporate mandate)
    ├── Procurement officer (public procurement authority delegation)
    ├── EBW technical mandate (COM(2025) 838 proposal)
    └── Digital EU Power of Attorney (Directive (EU) 2025/25)
```

| Dimension | Paradigm A — Natural-to-Natural | Paradigm B — Natural-to-Legal-Person |
|:----------|:-------------------------------|:-------------------------------------|
| **Legal/source basis** | eIDAS 2.0 representation concepts plus national family/civil law; operational credential semantics come from an accepted Topic 29 Rulebook | Directive (EU) 2025/25 for a digital EU PoA in specified cross-border company-law procedures; COM(2025) 838 for proposed EBW technical mandates/access control; national and sector law still governs authority |
| **Current ARF coverage** | Annex Topic 29 HLRs (`RP_01`, `RP_02`) permit scheme providers to create one or more natural-to-natural representation Rulebooks | No final ARF/EBW mandate credential profile; the Directive's PoA template and the proposed EBW access-control mandate are related but distinct artifacts |
| **Use cases** | Parent for minor, guardian for incapacitated adult, power of attorney for natural person | Company director, employee with signing authority, procurement officer acting for legal entity |
| **Issuance/creation authority** | Defined by the applicable Rulebook and underlying civil/family law source | Directive PoA: drawn up, amended, and revoked under national requirements with identity/capacity/authority verification by courts, notaries, or other competent authorities; proposed EBW technical mandate: granted by the Business Wallet owner |
| **Subject identifier** | `represented_entity_id` → links to the represented natural person's PID identifier under the final Rulebook | `represented_entity_id` → links to an LPID `legal_person_id` (EUID) |
| **Scope semantics** | Operations the representative may perform (e.g., "medical consent", "financial up to €10,000") — defined per Rulebook | Corporate authority scope (e.g., "contract signing", "procurement", "financial transactions") — linked to company register roles |
| **Projected VCT / type** | Future Rulebook-defined identifier; `eu.europa.ec.eudi.representation.1` is illustrative until assigned | Future EBW / mandate profile identifier; `eu.europa.ec.eudi.mandate.1` is illustrative until assigned |
| **Revocation model** | Multi-party: represented person, court, guardian authority | Multi-party: legal entity (board resolution), court, national register authority |
| **Cross-border** | Governed by the applicable national/international private-law framework; credential interoperability does not itself create authority | Directive PoA is evidence for procedures within Directive (EU) 2017/1132's scope; proposed EBW legal effect and mandate functions remain subject to the legislative outcome |

> **Current Topic 29 boundary**: Annex Topic 29 contains two substantive HLRs. `RP_01` permits Attestation Scheme Providers to create one or more Rulebooks for attestations issued to a natural person representing another natural person; every Rulebook must define its unique type and validity, nature of representation, and authorized operations. `RP_02` requires providers to make those attestations short-lived or revocable by all legally entitled entities. Topic 29 does not appoint the Commission as Rulebook publisher and does not govern EBW technical mandates or the Directive (EU) 2025/25 digital EU PoA.

##### 20.8.2 Mandate Credential Attribute Model

The model below is an **implementation envelope**, not a final ARF schema. Each Topic 29 natural-to-natural Rulebook must define its unique attestation type and validity, nature of representation, and authorised operations; it need not use these claim names or one shared schema. RPs can use the broader fields below for architecture planning and explicitly local test fixtures, but exact names, cardinality, selective-disclosure rules, VCT/docType values, trust sources, and status mechanisms remain Rulebook- or EBW-profile-defined.

**Common Attributes (Both Paradigms)**

| Attribute | Type | Planning status | Description |
|:----------|:-----|:----------------|:------------|
| `representation_type` | string enum | Rulebook-defined core for Topic 29 | Nature of the representation — e.g., `"parental_authority"`, `"legal_guardianship"`, `"power_of_attorney"`, `"corporate_mandate"` |
| `representative_id` | string | Expected binding field | Identifier of the representative — usually matched to the representative's PID subject identifier under the applicable Rulebook |
| `representative_name` | string | Expected display/audit field | Name of the representative — typically matched to PID name claims where disclosed |
| `represented_entity_type` | string enum | Expected discriminator | `"natural_person"` (Paradigm A) or `"legal_person"` (Paradigm B) |
| `represented_entity_id` | string | Expected binding field | Identifier of the represented entity — natural-person identifier (A) or `legal_person_id`/EUID (B) depending on the final profile |
| `represented_entity_name` | string | Expected display/audit field | Name of the represented entity |
| `scope_of_authority` | object | Rulebook-defined core for Topic 29 | Structured definition of authorised operations (§20.7.3) |
| `validity_period` | object | Rulebook-defined core for Topic 29 | `{ "not_before": datetime, "not_after": datetime }` or the final Rulebook equivalent |
| `issuing_authority` | string | Expected provenance field | Name/identifier of the entity that issued the mandate credential |
| `issuing_country` | string | Expected provenance field | ISO 3166-1 Alpha-2 country code |

**Paradigm B–Specific Attributes**

| Attribute | Type | Planning status | Description |
|:----------|:-----|:----------------|:------------|
| `corporate_role` | string | Projected EBW / corporate mandate field | Role within the legal entity (e.g., `"managing_director"`, `"procurator"`, `"authorised_signatory"`) |
| `registration_reference` | string | Projected EBW / register-link field | Reference to the company register entry granting authority (links to BRIS) |
| `joint_representation` | boolean | Projected governance field | `true` if this mandate requires joint exercise with another representative (Gesamtvertretung — see §20.6.3) |
| `joint_partner_ids` | array | Projected governance field | If `joint_representation` is true, identifiers of the other required representatives |
| `max_transaction_value` | object | Projected policy field | `{ "amount": number, "currency": "EUR" }` — monetary ceiling for financial operations |

**Projected SD-JWT VC Structure (Paradigm B)**

```json
{
  "vct": "eu.europa.ec.eudi.mandate.1",
  "iss": "https://mandate-provider.example.eu",
  "iat": 1711234567,
  "exp": 1742770567,
  "cnf": { "jwk": { "kty": "EC", "crv": "P-256", "x": "...", "y": "..." } },
  "representation_type": "corporate_mandate",
  "representative_id": "DE/ID/1234567890",
  "representative_name": "Anna Müller",
  "represented_entity_type": "legal_person",
  "represented_entity_id": "DEHRB.HRB12345",
  "represented_entity_name": "Beispiel GmbH",
  "corporate_role": "managing_director",
  "scope_of_authority": {
    "operations": ["contract_signing", "financial_transactions", "procurement_bidding"],
    "limitations": {
      "max_transaction_value": { "amount": 50000, "currency": "EUR" },
      "geographic_scope": "EU"
    },
    "exclusions": ["share_transfer", "liquidation"]
  },
  "validity_period": {
    "not_before": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "not_after": "2027-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  },
  "issuing_authority": "Handelsregister Berlin-Charlottenburg",
  "issuing_country": "DE",
  "registration_reference": "HRB 12345 B",
  "joint_representation": false,
  "status": {
    "status_list": {
      "uri": "https://mandate-provider.example.eu/status/mandate-list-1",
      "idx": 4832
    }
  }
}
```

> **Selective disclosure source-status note**: The Topic I discussion paper proposed non-concealable representation and scope fields. Current Annex Topic 29 requires each applicable Rulebook to define representation attributes, but it does not itself publish final selective-disclosure rules. RPs should plan to require the representation nature, authorised operations, and binding identifiers whenever they are necessary to decide the transaction, while treating exact disclosure requirements as Rulebook-defined.

##### 20.8.3 Natural-to-Natural Representation (Paradigm A)

Current Annex Topic 29 permits Attestation Scheme Providers to create one or more Rulebooks for a **natural person acting on behalf of another natural person**—for example, a parent acting for a minor, a legal guardian for an incapacitated person, or a power-of-attorney holder. The historical Topic I discussion paper remains useful background, but the current normative surface is narrower: every created Rulebook must define a unique attestation type and validity plus the nature of representation and authorised operations.

**Legal Basis:**
- eIDAS 2.0 Art. 3(1), 3(3), 3(4), 3(5a), 5a(5)(f), 11a(3)(c), Annex VI §10
- Brussels IIb Regulation — cross-border parental authority for minors
- Hague Convention 2000 — cross-border guardianship/PoA for incapacitated adults

**RP implementation implications:**

1. **The RP must detect representative capacity** rather than treating the presenter as the represented person. Each accepted Rulebook must define a unique attestation type; the RP resolves that type through the relevant catalogue/profile rather than assuming one EU-wide `vct` or `docType`.

2. **Scope restrictions are embedded in the attestation.** The attestation includes attributes defining:
   - The **nature of the representation** (e.g., parental authority, guardianship, power of attorney)
   - The **operations the representative is authorised to perform** (e.g., "medical consent", "financial transactions up to €10,000")
   - The **identity of the represented person** (the beneficiary)

3. **Heightened revocation scrutiny.** `RP_02` requires the provider to ensure that natural-to-natural representation attestations are either short-lived or revocable by all legally entitled entities. RPs should treat representation status freshness with elevated urgency because a revoked representation means the presenter no longer has authority to act.

4. **DCQL query implications.** If the RP's DCQL query requests a standard PID, and the Wallet holds only a representation PID, the response will contain the representation attestation type. The RP must:
   - Detect the type difference (the `vct`/`docType` will not match a standard PID type)
   - Adjust processing logic accordingly (e.g., display "Acting on behalf of [represented person]")
   - Verify the representation scope permits the requested operation
   - Never treat the presenter's identity as interchangeable with the represented person's identity

**DCQL Query Pattern (Paradigm A — projected type)**

The `vct` and claim paths below are illustrative. A production query must use the exact type and schema from one accepted, versioned Rulebook.

```json
{
  "credentials": [
    {
      "id": "representation",
      "format": "dc+sd-jwt",
      "meta": { "vct_values": ["eu.europa.ec.eudi.representation.1"] },
      "claims": [
        {"path": ["representation_type"]},
        {"path": ["representative_id"]},
        {"path": ["represented_entity_id"]},
        {"path": ["represented_entity_name"]},
        {"path": ["scope_of_authority"]},
        {"path": ["legal_basis"]}
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "representative_pid",
      "format": "dc+sd-jwt",
      "meta": { "vct_values": ["urn:eudi:pid:1"] },
      "claims": [
        {"path": ["family_name"]},
        {"path": ["given_name"]},
        {"path": ["birthdate"]}
      ]
    }
  ],
  "credential_sets": [
    {
      "purpose": "Verify representative identity and authority to act for represented person",
      "options": [["representation", "representative_pid"]]
    }
  ]
}
```

> **Cross-references**: §19.5 (combined presentations — a representation attestation may appear alongside a standard PID in a combined query), §24.1 (CDD — representation may affect KYC obligations, e.g., onboarding a minor's account), §23.3 (GDPR — processing for a represented minor may have a different legal basis under Art. 8).

##### 20.8.4 Natural-to-Legal-Person Mandates (Paradigm B)

**Paradigm B** covers a natural person acting on behalf of a **legal person** — a company director executing contracts, a procurement officer submitting bids, an employee authorising financial transactions. This is the primary B2B mandate use case and the more complex paradigm.

**Legal Basis:**
- COM(2025) 838 — European Business Wallet regulation proposal (November 2025)
- Directive (EU) 2025/25 — in-force company-law digital-tools amendment establishing a digital EU power-of-attorney template for specified cross-border procedures
- National company and sector law — continues to govern the underlying authority, legal capacity, and permitted acts

**Corporate Mandate Use Cases:**

| Use Case | Representative | Required policy question | Possible evidence composition |
|:---------|:--------------|:-------------------------|:------------------------------|
| **Contract signing** | Company director or delegate | Does the governing mandate/PoA and company law authorize this contract and value? | Representative identity + current entity evidence + accepted authority artifact |
| **Procurement bidding** | Procurement officer | Does the mandate cover this procedure, lot, jurisdiction, and deadline? | Profile-defined mandate plus procurement-specific evidence |
| **Financial operations** | CFO / authorised signatory | Is this transaction and amount within current authority and sector controls? | Identity/entity/authority evidence plus applicable financial controls |
| **Company-law filing** | Company representative | Is the procedure within Directive (EU) 2017/1132 / Article 16c scope and the PoA template? | Digital EU PoA plus the identity and register evidence required by the procedure |

**Digital EU Power of Attorney (Directive (EU) 2025/25) and EBW Mandates (COM(2025) 838)**

Directive (EU) 2025/25 inserts Article 16c into Directive (EU) 2017/1132. It requires Member States to let covered companies use a common digital EU power-of-attorney template to authorize a person for specified cross-border company-law procedures, including company formation, branch registration/closure, and cross-border conversions, mergers, and divisions:

1. **Common multilingual template** — the Commission establishes the template and technical specifications through implementing acts
2. **National-law creation and control** — drawing up, amendment, and revocation follow national requirements; courts, notaries, or other competent authorities verify the grantor's identity, legal capacity, and authority to represent the company
3. **Trust-service authentication and EUDI compatibility** — the PoA must be authenticated with eIDAS trust services and be compatible with the European Digital Identity Wallet
4. **Defined evidentiary scope** — it is accepted as evidence of the authorization stated in the document for the Directive's procedures; it does not replace all national rules on representation or create a general financial/contractual mandate vocabulary

COM(2025) 838 is a separate, ongoing proposal. It defines an EBW mandate as authorization granted by a Business Wallet owner to an authorized representative to operate functions of a designated wallet and proposes role/mandate-based access control. Its recitals call for compatibility with the Directive's digital EU PoA. Do not collapse the Directive's external company-law evidence artifact into the proposal's internal/technical wallet mandate or predict final adoption dates.

**DCQL Query Patterns for Paradigm B** — see §20.6 for the triple-credential DCQL (LPID + PID + mandate) and the mandate-only DCQL query.

##### 20.8.5 Mandate Verification Flow

The following Mermaid sequence diagram illustrates the RP's verification flow when receiving a triple-credential corporate presentation (LPID + PID + mandate). This extends the combined presentation verification flow in §19.4 with mandate-specific verification steps (phases 4–5).

```mermaid
---

  themeVariables:
    noteBkgColor: "transparent"
    noteBorderColor: "transparent"
  sequence:
    messageAlign: left
    noteAlign: left
    actorMargin: 250
---
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant RP as 🏦 RP Instance
    participant SL as 📋 Profile-Selected<br/>Status Evidence

    rect rgba(148, 163, 184, 0.14)
    Note right of RP: Phase 1: Response Parsing
    RP->>RP: Decrypt JWE, extract vp_token<br/>containing LPID + PID + mandate
    RP->>RP: Identify credential types<br/>from vct/docType values
    Note right of SL: ⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀

        RP->>RP: Verify issuer signature<br/>(profile-authorized trust source)
        RP->>RP: Validate claims (exp, iat, vct)
        RP->>RP: Verify selective disclosures
        RP->>RP: Verify device binding<br/>(KB-JWT / DeviceAuth)
        RP->>SL: Evaluate selected status<br/>or short-lived branch
        SL-->>RP: Profile-scoped result

    RP->>RP: Verify mandate.represented_entity_id<br/>== lpid.legal_person_id (EUID)

    RP->>RP: Log mandate verification<br/>for audit trail (§33.3)
    Note right of SL: ⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
```
