#### 28.2 Regulatory Mandate and Compliance Timeline

Banks and PSPs are among the first private-sector entities legally obligated to accept EUDI Wallets. This obligation emerges from the intersection of three regulatory frameworks:

##### 28.2.1 Wallet Acceptance Timeline at a Glance

Read the timeline as a **wallet-acceptance-status** diagram, not as an internal build plan. It highlights the hard date-driven milestones for Bank/PSP use: when certified wallets become available, when general wallet acceptance becomes practically possible, when PID-based CDD becomes operationally available under the AMLR, and when private-sector EUDI Wallet SCA acceptance becomes mandatory. Pseudonym and progressive-assurance support are part of the same acceptance surface, but they are service-conditional rather than a single fixed milestone, so they are summarised in the use-case matrix below instead of as a separate Gantt bar.

```mermaid
gantt
    title Bank/PSP EUDI Wallet Acceptance Timeline
    dateFormat YYYY-MM-DD
    axisFormat %b %Y

    section Legal Milestones
    Certified wallets available (Art. 5a)             :milestone, m0, 2026-12-24, 0d
    WRP registration rules apply (CIR 2025/848)       :milestone, mreg, 2026-12-24, 0d
    AMLR CDD applicability (Art. 22(6)(b))           :milestone, m1, 2027-07-10, 0d
    eIDAS Art. 5f(2) mandatory acceptance             :milestone, m2, 2027-12-24, 0d

    section Voluntary / Permitted
    Early-adoption window for wallet acceptance       :active, vol, 2026-12-24, 2027-12-24
    PID-based CDD operationally available             :active, cdd, 2027-07-10, 2028-06-30

    section Mandatory
    EUDI Wallet SCA acceptance mandatory              :crit, sca, 2027-12-24, 2028-06-30
```

| Use case | Earliest practical use | Mandatory / conditional posture | Legal basis | Detailed coverage |
|:---------|:-----------------------|:--------------------------------|:------------|:------------------|
| **PID / CDD onboarding** | **10 July 2027** | Permitted and strongly expected; becomes difficult to justify refusing once the PSP can already verify wallet presentations operationally | AMLR 2024/1624 Art. 22(6)(b), Recital 66 | Customer Due Diligence (AML/KYC) (§28.5.1); Identity Matching (CIR 2025/846) (§28.5.2) |
| **Pseudonym / progressive assurance** | **24 December 2026** for services that do not legally require identification | Conditional: RPs must not refuse pseudonyms where identification is not required by Union or national law; step up to PID only when the service requires it | eIDAS Reg. Art. 5b(9); CIR 2024/2979 Art. 14, Annex V; ARF Annex 2 Topic 11 | Pseudonym Acceptance and Progressive Assurance (§28.3.2); Progressive Assurance: Register Low, Verify Identity, Authenticate High (§18.13) |
| **SCA acceptance** | **24 December 2026** for voluntary pilots; **24 December 2027** for mandatory acceptance | Mandatory on user request wherever Art. 5f(2) and the PSD2/PSR SCA triggers apply | eIDAS Reg. Art. 5f(2); PSD2 Art. 97; RTS Art. 13, Art. 24 | eIDAS Trigger: Article 5f(2) (§28.2.2); SCA Programme: Issuance, Presentation, Dynamic Linking, and RTS Evidence (§28.4) |

| Milestone | Date | Source |
|:----------|:-----|:-------|
| First wallet core/certification implementing acts enter into force | 24 December 2024 | CIR 2024/2977-2982, incl. CIR 2024/2981 Art. 22 and CIR 2024/2982 Art. 8 |
| Certified EUDI Wallets available | 24 December 2026 | eIDAS Reg. Art. 5a: Member States must provide wallets within 24 months of IAs |
| WRP registration rules apply | 24 December 2026 | CIR 2025/848 Art. 11 |
| **Early-adoption window opens** | **24 December 2026** | **No prohibition on voluntary acceptance once certified wallets exist** |
| AMLR CDD applicability | 10 July 2027 | AMLR 2024/1624 Art. 22(6)(b) |
| Public sector mandatory acceptance | 24 December 2026 | eIDAS Reg. Art. 5f(1): 24 months after IAs |
| **Private sector (incl. Banks/PSPs) mandatory acceptance** | **24 December 2027** | **eIDAS Reg. Art. 5f(2): 36 months after implementing acts** |

> **Early-adoption window (~12 months):** Art. 5f(2) sets a *deadline* ("no later than 36 months"), not a *start date*. Once certified wallets become available by 24 December 2026, nothing in the regulation prohibits private RPs from accepting them voluntarily. PSPs that go live during this window gain competitive advantage: early movers capture wallet-native customers, build operational experience before the compliance cliff, and can iterate on UX before the mandatory deadline forces a rush deployment. That same window is where PSPs can bring up pseudonym-friendly pre-identification journeys and prepare the PID verification pipeline before AMLR CDD use becomes operational on 10 July 2027.

> **Registrar timing:** Do not read the Gantt as saying that registration work starts only on 1 January 2027. CIR 2025/848 applies from 24 December 2026, and the Commission's [RP Registration Service Reference Implementation](https://docs.eudi.dev/0.5/build/supporting-ecosystem-services/rp-registration-service/) already supports experimentation, but that service is expressly non-production. The practical plan is therefore: prepare legal identifiers, use-case declarations, contact data, key-management choices, and trust-list integration in Q4 2026; complete production registration and WRPAC onboarding as national registrars and authorised certificate providers open.

Banks and PSPs face two hard date-driven regulatory tracks, plus a separate service-conditional acceptance surface for pseudonym-friendly journeys. Treating the wallet as "SCA-only" is a strategic error — the Anti-Money Laundering Regulation (AMLR 2024/1624) strongly enables wallet-based CDD/KYC five months before the eIDAS SCA mandate takes effect, while Art. 5b(9) separately prohibits refusing pseudonyms where legal identification is not required.

| Date-driven track | Legal Basis | Deadline | Nature | Scope |
|:------------------|:-----------|:---------|:-------|:------|
| **CDD/KYC** | AMLR 2024/1624 Art. 22(6)(b) + Recital 66 | **10 July 2027** | Permitted & recommended | Remote onboarding, identity verification, ongoing CDD |
| **SCA** | eIDAS Reg. Art. 5f(2) + PSD2 Art. 97 | **24 December 2027** | **Mandatory** | Payment authentication, account access, remote actions, PSC association |

> **Legal precision**: The AMLR does not contain a standalone "shall accept" clause for wallet-based CDD. Art. 22(6)(b) lists eIDAS electronic identification (including EUDI Wallet) as one of two *permitted* verification methods ("through **either** of the following means"). Recital 66 uses stronger language — the wallet "should be taken into account and **accepted** by obliged entities" — but Recitals are interpretive, not operative. The *mandatory* acceptance obligation comes from eIDAS Art. 5f(2), not the AMLR. However, once obliged entities are technically capable of verifying PIDs for the SCA track, refusing wallet-based CDD becomes indefensible: the Recital expectation, the risk-reduction incentive (Art. 22(6)(b) reduces risk to "standard or low"), and the reputational cost of rejecting a Commission-endorsed identification method create a *de facto* obligation.

> **⚠️ Timeline reality check (checked 26 July 2026):** Registration and trust-infrastructure preparation can start before the formal AMLR/eIDAS application dates, but the legal dates remain fixed: AMLR CDD applicability starts on **10 July 2027**, and private-sector EUDI Wallet SCA acceptance becomes mandatory on **24 December 2027**. A PSP should assess delivery readiness against its actual registration, supplier, certification, and test evidence; the 2027 legal acceptance obligation is not already in force.

##### 28.2.2 eIDAS Trigger: Article 5f(2)

The mandatory acceptance obligation for Banks and PSPs is rooted in **Article 5f(2) of the eIDAS Regulation (as amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183)**:

> Where private relying parties that provide services, with the exception of microenterprises and small enterprises [...], are required by Union or national law to use strong user authentication for online identification or where strong user authentication for online identification is required by contractual obligation, **including in the areas of** transport, energy, **banking, financial services**, social security, health, drinking water, postal services, digital infrastructure, education or telecommunications, those private relying parties shall [...] also accept European Digital Identity Wallets that are provided in accordance with this Regulation.
>
> — *Article 5f(2), Regulation (EU) 2024/1183*

Banks and PSPs are explicitly named sectors. Since PSD2 Article 97 (and its successor, the PSR) mandates Strong Customer Authentication for electronic payments and account access, every PSP that performs SCA is within scope of Art. 5f(2).

The European Commission's EUDIW FAQ leaves no room for ambiguity on this point:

> *"As per Article 5f(2) of Regulation (EU) No 910/2014, certain private relying parties are required to accept the wallets, upon request of the user, where Strong Customer Authentication (SCA) is required by Union or national law, or by contractual obligation. For example, under the PSD2 Directive, payment service providers are required to apply SCA in specific situations. This obligation to accept the wallets upon request of the user applies 36 months after the entry into force of the implementing acts referred to in Article 5a(23) and Article 5c(6) of Regulation (EU) No 910/2014."*
>
> — [EC EUDIW FAQ — Is there an obligation to accept EU Digital Identity Wallets in the area of banking and financial services?](https://ec.europa.eu/digital-building-blocks/sites/spaces/EUDIGITALIDENTITYWALLET/pages/713526976/FAQ)

Note that the obligation extends beyond statutory SCA requirements — it also covers cases where SCA is required **by contractual obligation** (e.g., internal risk policies, card scheme rules, or acquirer agreements that mandate SCA beyond PSD2 minimum thresholds).

##### 28.2.3 PSD2/PSR Bridge: SCA as the Trigger

PSD2 Article 97(1) and RTS Articles 13 and 24 require SCA for:
- **(a)** accessing a payment account online,
- **(b)** initiating an electronic payment transaction,
- **(c)** carrying out any action through a remote channel which may imply a risk of payment fraud — including granting AISP/PISP consent, managing trusted beneficiary lists (RTS Art. 13(1)), and payment instrument management, and
- **(d)** associating PSCs or authentication devices with the user via a remote channel (RTS Art. 24(2)(b)) — i.e., authenticator binding / authenticator enrollment.

Since PSD2/PSR requires "strong user authentication" (the equivalent of eIDAS 2.0's "strong user authentication" — Art. 3(51)), PSPs are captured by eIDAS Reg. Art. 5f(2) regardless of whether they otherwise wish to integrate EUDI Wallets.

> **Terminology clarification — SUA vs. SCA**: The eIDAS Regulation uses "strong **user** authentication" (SUA) while PSD2 uses "strong **customer** authentication" (SCA). These are synonyms. The European Commission's official EUDIW FAQ clarifies:
>
> *"Since EU Digital Identity Wallets are provided free of charge and do not involve customers in the traditional sense, Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 consistently refers to their holders as 'users' instead of 'customers'. Although the terms differ, both refer to the same underlying concept, a multi-factor authentication process that ensures secure and reliable user authentication and should therefore be considered as synonyms in this context."*
>
> — [EC Digital Building Blocks — EUDIW FAQ](https://ec.europa.eu/digital-building-blocks/sites/spaces/EUDIGITALIDENTITYWALLET/pages/713526976/FAQ)

Both are defined identically: authentication based on at least two independent factors from the categories knowledge, possession, and inherence (eIDAS Reg. Art. 3(51); PSD2 Art. 4(30)). This specification uses **SCA** when discussing PSD2/PSR payment obligations and **SUA** when discussing the eIDAS 2.0 mandate — but PSPs should treat them as interchangeable.

##### 28.2.4 Financial Services Use Cases Under Recital 62

Recital 62 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 explicitly ratifies this intersection:

> Secure electronic identification and the provision of attestation of attributes should offer additional flexibility and solutions for the financial services sector to allow the identification of customers and the exchange of specific attributes necessary to comply with, for example, **customer due diligence requirements** under a future Regulation establishing the Anti Money Laundering Authority, with **suitability requirements** stemming from investor protection law, or to support the fulfilment of **strong customer authentication requirements** for online identification for the purposes of **account login and of initiation of transactions** in the field of payment services.
>
> — *Recital 62, Regulation (EU) 2024/1183*

This recital confirms three distinct financial use cases for EUDI Wallets:
1. **AML/CDD** — customer identity verification for account opening and ongoing monitoring
2. **Investor suitability** — MiFID II suitability attribute exchange
3. **SCA for payments** — identity verification for account login and transaction initiation

##### 28.2.5 Parallel Delivery Workstreams

The PID verification pipeline (§13) must be operational before production SCA Attestation use, because Wallet SCA depends on the PSP being able to recognise and bind the correct customer. That does **not** mean the build should be waterfall, and it also does **not** move the legal start dates forward. CDD implementation work can run before 10 July 2027; wallet-based CDD operation under the AMLR starts on 10 July 2027. TS12/SCA implementation work can run before December 2027; mandatory EUDI Wallet SCA acceptance starts on 24 December 2027. This dual-track reality drives the recommended workstream plan:

> **Upstream issuance enabler — CIR 2026/798**: The April 2026 remote-onboarding act does not change the RP-side deadlines in this timeline, but it materially improves the **supply-side path** for wallet issuance: Member States can now rely on a harmonised route where an existing eID at **LoA substantial** is combined with additional remote onboarding procedures to reach **LoA high**. For banks and PSPs, that does not remove PID verification, revocation checking, or CDD obligations; it does mean that remotely issued, high-assurance Wallet/PID populations are more defensible as an onboarding basis.

**Parallel Workstream Checklist:**

| Workstream | Deliverable | Dependencies / coupling | Target |
|:------|:----------|:-------------|:-------|
| **Registration** | Prepare RP registration pack; register with national Registrar; obtain WRPAC | Business decision to accept EUDI Wallet; production issuance depends on national registrar / authorised WRPAC provider opening | Q4 2026-Q1 2027 |
| **DORA / Operational Readiness** | Include EUDI Wallet in digital resilience testing; assess intermediary risk | Starts with architecture/vendor decisions and continues through operational readiness | Q1-Q4 2027 |
| **Trust Infrastructure** | Pre-cache LoTE/Trusted Lists; implement refresh mechanism | Sandbox/reference integration can start before production sources; production trust validation depends on national trust sources being available | Q4 2026-Q2 2027 |
| **SCA implementation preparation** | Implement TS12 SCA with `transaction_data` and Dynamic Linking | TS12 design can start once the issuer model and wallet specs are selected; this is preparation, not a January 2027 legal acceptance start | Q1-Q4 2027; mandatory acceptance from **24 Dec 2027** |
| **Core Protocol** | Implement OID4VP 1.0 (JAR, DCQL, direct_post.jwt) for both SD-JWT and mdoc | Registration/trust work underway; protocol stack can be built against reference wallets and sandboxes | Q1-Q2 2027 |
| **CDD implementation preparation** ⬅️ AMLR applicability | Build CDD onboarding with PID presentation + AML screening | PID verification path, matching policy, AML screening integration, and fallback process; this is preparation before the AMLR date | Q1-Q2 2027; wallet-based CDD operation from **10 Jul 2027** |
| **Pseudonym Support** | Implement WebAuthn/passkey pseudonym route where the current profile applies, plus progressive assurance and a Topic 11 abstraction for later pseudonym mechanisms | Service-policy classification and account-linking model | Q1-Q3 2027 |
| **Testing** | End-to-end testing with EU Reference Wallet + national sandbox | Starts with protocol skeleton and continues as CDD/SCA/pseudonym flows become available | Q1-Q4 2027 |
| **Production** ⬅️ eIDAS deadline | Go-live before mandatory acceptance deadline | All testing passed | **Before 24 Dec 2027** |
| **Corporate** | Add LPID and representation support for corporate onboarding | Availability of the selected LPID, representation, digital EU PoA, or final EBW profile and its production trust/status sources | Profile- and jurisdiction-gated; no fixed deployment date is established |

> **Strategic note**: PSPs that delay implementation pending "further clarity" on peripheral issues (SCA Attestation Rulebook, PSR/PSD3 RTS) assume significant regulatory risk. The core obligations — CDD via PID and SCA via TS12 — are technically specified and legally certain. See §28.9 for the full inventory of industry disputes and open questions.


#### 28.3 Wallet Acceptance Baseline for Banks and PSPs

These baseline obligations make the bank or PSP a valid Wallet RP before the specialised SCA, CDD, resilience, or extended-use-case controls are layered on top. Each row links its regulatory basis and the DR-0002 section containing the detailed implementation guidance.

##### 28.3.1 RP Registration and Trust Establishment

🔴 **Mandatory** — All banks and PSPs accepting EUDI Wallet presentations

Banks and PSPs must register as Relying Parties before they can accept EUDI Wallet presentations. This is not optional — it is a precondition for receiving a Wallet-Relying Party Access Certificate (WRPAC), which is required for mutual authentication with the Wallet Unit.

| # | Obligation | Regulatory Basis | DR-0002 Reference |
|:-:|:-----------|:-----------------|:------------------|
| 1 | Register with national Registrar before accepting EUDI Wallet presentations | eIDAS Reg. Art. 5b(1) | RP Registration, Data Model, and Registrar API (§4); Certificate Hierarchy and Trust Chains (§5.1) |
| 2 | Declare all intended data requests (PID attributes, SCA attestation types) at registration | eIDAS Reg. Art. 5b(2)(c) | RP Registration Baseline and ETSI TS 119 475 Overlay (§4.2) |
| 3 | Request only declared data — no over-requesting beyond registration scope | eIDAS Reg. Art. 5b(3) | Registration Process Overview (§4.3); RP Obligations: Data Deletion, DPA Reporting, and Disclosure Policy (§22) |
| 4 | Obtain WRPAC from an Access Certificate Authority | CIR 2025/848 Art. 7 | Access Certificates (WRPAC) (§5.2) |
| 5 | Identify PSP to Wallet User at presentation time (via WRPAC) | eIDAS Reg. Art. 5b(8) | WRPAC Usage in Protocols (§5.2.3) |
| 6 | Provide privacy policy URL for each intended use | CIR 2025/848 Art. 8(2)(g) | Registration Certificates (WRPRC) (§5.3) |
| 7 | Notify Registrar of changes to registration data without delay | eIDAS Reg. Art. 5b(6), CIR 2025/848 Art. 5(3) | Registrar REST API (§4.4) |
| 8 | Provide complete Annex I information in machine-readable format | CIR 2025/848 Art. 5(1), Annex I | RP Registration Baseline and ETSI TS 119 475 Overlay (§4.2) |
| 9 | Ensure registration information accuracy at time of submission | CIR 2025/848 Art. 5(2) | RP Registration Baseline and ETSI TS 119 475 Overlay (§4.2) |
| 10 | Register appropriate entitlement type(s): `Service_Provider`, `QEAA_Provider` | CIR 2025/848 Annex I point 12 | RP Registration Baseline and ETSI TS 119 475 Overlay (§4.2) |
| 11 | Notify registrar and request cancellation when ceasing wallet use | CIR 2025/848 Art. 6(7) | Registrar REST API (§4.4) |
| 12 | Maintain alternative authentication means — EUDI Wallet is additive, not a replacement | eIDAS Reg. Art. 5a(15) | Shared Trust Infrastructure (§20.2) |
| 13 | Be prepared for user-initiated reporting to data protection authorities via wallet | CIR 2024/2982 Art. 7(1) | GDPR Obligations for RPs (§23.3) |

> **eIDAS Reg. Art. 5b(2) — Full legal text**:
>
> The registration process shall be cost-effective and proportionate-to-risk. The relying party shall provide at least: (a) the information necessary to authenticate to European Digital Identity Wallets [...]; (b) the contact details of the relying party; (c) the intended use of European Digital Identity Wallets, including an indication of the data to be requested by the relying party from users.

**Bank-specific note**: PSPs typically need to register multiple intended uses: SCA for payments (`transaction_data` with payment context), CDD for account opening (full PID), and potentially ongoing re-verification. Each intended use maps to a distinct set of requested attributes. Structure registration data accordingly — a single "banking" registration with all PID attributes declared will trigger data minimisation scrutiny.

At the same time, banks and PSPs often operate a second certificate layer toward payment/open-banking infrastructure. That adjacent layer should be read as follows:

| Surface | PSD2/open-banking meaning under `ETSI TS 119 495` | What it does **not** replace in the Wallet stack |
|:--------|:---------------------------------------------------|:--------------------------------------------------|
| `QWAC` | Institution-facing TLS/authentication certificate profile for bank/PSP channels | `WRPAC` authentication of the wallet-facing presenter |
| `QSealC` | Institution-facing signing/sealing certificate profile for PSP messages and artefacts | `WRPRC` or national-register authorization data for wallet attribute requests |
| Open-banking `QCStatement` | Certificate-carried role/authority payload including `rolesOfPSP`, `NCAName`, and `NCAId` | Wallet request scope, intended-use declarations, or TS12 SCA transaction binding |
| `organizationIdentifier` / `PSD` authorization number | ETSI EN 319 412-1 / TS 119 495 identifier syntax for a PSP authorization number under PSD2 or equivalent national/international legislation, interpreted with NCA-shaped register context | The shared WRPAC/WRPRC subject-linkage semantics used by Wallet RP registration, or live proof of current PSP role authorization without NCA/EBA register validation |
| NCA/EBA register checks and NCA-triggered revocation | Live authorization-state and certificate-status confirmation layer for PSP roles | Self-sufficient proof from certificate fields alone |
| `VoP` role additions | Extension of the same open-banking role vocabulary for Verification of Payee services (`VOP_RS`, `VOP_VS`) | A new Wallet RP entitlement or wallet-protocol role |

Operationally, the bank should parse the certificate-carried open-banking fields, but still treat current authorization state as a **register-backed** question. `rolesOfPSP`, `NCAName`, `NCAId`, `organizationIdentifier`, and any `VoP` role indicators are evidence carried in the certificate profile; they become trustworthy only when interpreted together with the relevant home-NCA or EBA register view, and with authenticated revocation or status updates from the competent-authority side.

##### 28.3.2 Pseudonym Acceptance and Progressive Assurance

🔴 **Mandatory** — All banks and PSPs accepting EUDI Wallet presentations

Banks and PSPs must accept pseudonymous authentication for services that do not legally require identity verification.

| # | Obligation | Regulatory Basis | DR-0002 Reference |
|:-:|:-----------|:-----------------|:------------------|
| 1 | Accept pseudonyms where legal identification is not required | eIDAS Reg. Art. 5b(9) | Pseudonym-Based Authentication and WebAuthn (§18) |
| 2 | Do not prohibit pseudonym use for general account browsing / service discovery | eIDAS Reg. Art. 5, Recital 60 | Pseudonym Overview (§18.1) |
| 3 | Implement a WebAuthn/passkey pseudonym registration route where the current Topic 11 profile applies | CIR 2024/2979 Art. 14, Annex V; Annex Topic 11 `PA_21`-`PA_22` | Pseudonym Registration and Authentication Flow (§18.6) |
| 4 | Support progressive assurance: pseudonym → full PID when escalation is required | — (architectural best practice) | Progressive Assurance: Register Low, Verify Identity, Authenticate High (§18.13) |

> **eIDAS Reg. Art. 5b(9) — Full legal text**:
>
> Relying parties shall be responsible for carrying out the procedure for authenticating and validating person identification data and electronic attestation of attributes requested from European Digital Identity Wallets. **Relying parties shall not refuse the use of pseudonyms, where the identification of the user is not required by Union or national law.**

**Bank-specific application**: This creates a nuanced obligation for PSPs. For services subject to AML/CDD (account opening, transactions), legal identification IS required — pseudonyms are not applicable. However, for pre-authentication services (product browsing, rate comparison, general information), PSPs cannot force PID presentation. The recommended architectural pattern is **progressive assurance** (§18.13):

1. **Pseudonym-only** — User browses products, compares rates, uses calculators → WebAuthn pseudonym only
2. **Attribute step-up** — User requests a personalised quote requiring age/income bracket → dedicated age evidence or PID `birthdate` fallback with local threshold computation
3. **Full identification** — User initiates account opening → full PID presentation for CDD
4. **SCA binding** — Ongoing transaction authentication → SCA attestation linked to the verified identity

Each escalation step preserves the pseudonym binding, allowing the bank to maintain session continuity without re-authentication. See §18.13 for the complete progressive assurance protocol.

##### 28.3.3 Channel Coverage and User-Choice Rule

🔴 **Mandatory** — All PSPs offering digital channels where SCA is required

The legal chain is precise: PSD2 Art. 97(1) defines three mandatory SCA triggers. Art. 5f(2) mandates that wherever strong user authentication is already legally or contractually required, the PSP must **also accept** EUDI Wallets — **"only upon the voluntary request of the user"**:

> **Art. 5f(2)** (emphasis added): *"Where private relying parties that provide services, with the exception of microenterprises and small enterprises [...], **are required by Union or national law to use strong user authentication for online identification or where strong user authentication for online identification is required by contractual obligation**, including in the areas of transport, energy, banking, financial services, social security, health, drinking water, postal services, digital infrastructure, education or telecommunications, those private relying parties shall [...] **only upon the voluntary request of the user, also accept European Digital Identity Wallets** that are provided in accordance with this Regulation."*

This means EUDI Wallet SCA must be offered as a **user-choosable alternative** alongside existing SCA methods (SMS OTP, hardware token, banking app push), not a mandatory replacement. The user selects whether to use the EUDI Wallet or their existing SCA method.

The PSD2 Art. 97(1) SCA triggers and the RTS Art. 24(2)(b) PSC association trigger where EUDI Wallet acceptance becomes mandatory:

| # | Trigger | Legal Basis | EUDI Wallet SCA Application | DR-0002 Reference |
|:-:|:--------|:------------|:---------------------------|:------------------:|
| (a) | **Accessing a payment account online** | PSD2 Art. 97(1)(a) | User chooses EUDI Wallet for login authentication → SCA attestation presentation | SCA Attestation Context (§17.1) |
| (b) | **Initiating an electronic payment transaction** | PSD2 Art. 97(1)(b) | User chooses EUDI Wallet for payment authorisation → `transaction_data` with Dynamic Linking | Payment Payload JSON Schema (TS12 Normative) (§17.14); Transactional Data HLRs (Topic 20) (§17.15) |
| (c₁) | **Granting TPP consent** — authorising an AISP or PISP to access account data or initiate payments | PSD2 Art. 97(1)(c) | User authenticates to ASPSP via EUDI Wallet to authorize TPP access. Re-authentication required periodically (every 180 days for AISP) | PSD2/PSR and SCA Bridge (§23.2) |
| (c₂) | **Managing trusted beneficiary lists** — creating, amending, or deleting whitelisted payees | RTS Art. 13(1) | User authenticates via EUDI Wallet when adding a payee to the trusted list. Subsequent payments to that payee may then be SCA-exempt | PSD2/PSR and SCA Bridge (§23.2) |
| (c₃) | **Other remote actions implying fraud risk** — credential registration, payment instrument management, account settings changes | PSD2 Art. 97(1)(c) | Catch-all: any PSP action with fraud risk must offer EUDI Wallet as SCA option | OID4VCI Issuance Flow for SCA Attestations (§17.4); PSD2/PSR and SCA Bridge (§23.2) |
| (d) | **PSC Association / authenticator binding** — associating user identity with new credentials, authentication devices, or software via remote channel | RTS Art. 24(2)(b), Art. 26 | Existing customer presents PID or SCA Attestation to bootstrap authenticator on new device, replacing legacy re-enrollment (SMS OTP, branch visit) | OID4VCI Issuance Flow for SCA Attestations (§17.4) |

All triggers independently require the PSP to offer EUDI Wallet SCA. A PSP cannot selectively offer Wallet SCA for payments (trigger b) but refuse it for account login (trigger a) or TPP consent (trigger c₁).

**Channel delivery**: The PSP must offer EUDI Wallet SCA on every digital channel where it currently offers services:

| Channel | Protocol | DR-0002 Reference |
|:--------|:---------|:------------------|
| **Mobile banking app** | Same-device flow via W3C DC API / Android CredentialManager | Same-Device Remote Presentation (§11) |
| **Web banking (desktop/laptop)** | Prefer DC API-mediated same-device or secure local cross-device presentation where supported; retain QR + `request_uri` as a controlled compatibility/accessibility branch | Same-Device Remote Presentation (§11); Cross-Device Remote Presentation (§12) |

If a PSP offers both mobile and web banking, it must support EUDI Wallet SCA on both. See §11.3 for platform-specific considerations (notably the Safari DC API limitation for iOS web flows).


#### 28.4 SCA Programme: Issuance, Presentation, Dynamic Linking, and RTS Evidence

The TS12 payment authentication flow is the central PSP-specific runtime obligation. PSPs must implement the EUDI Wallet as an SCA method for every covered SCA trigger: account access, payment initiation, fraud-risk remote actions, and remote association or renewal of personalised security credentials, authentication devices, or authentication software.

That runtime flow sits inside a wider PSD2/RTS control wrapper. A PSP must also govern payment-instrument issuance, personalised-security-credential association, transaction monitoring, SCA exemptions, evidence retention, dispute proof, liability handling, and open-banking interface parity. The Wallet can carry and present the SCA Attestation, but the PSP still owns the regulated payment-service decision and the records needed to defend it.

##### 28.4.1 SCA Trigger Scope and Obligations

🔴 **Mandatory** — All PSPs performing Strong Customer Authentication under PSD2 Art. 97 and RTS authenticator-association rules

| # | Obligation | Regulatory Basis | DR-0002 Reference |
|:-:|:-----------|:-----------------|:------------------|
| 1 | Accept EUDI Wallet for SCA across all covered triggers: account login, payment initiation, fraud-risk remote actions, and remote PSC/authenticator association | eIDAS Reg. Art. 5f(2) + PSD2 Art. 97(1) + RTS Art. 24(2)(b), Art. 26 | SCA for Electronic Payments: Lifecycle, Flows, and Dynamic Linking (§17); PSD2/PSR and SCA Bridge (§23.2); Channel Coverage and User-Choice Rule (§28.3.3); SCA Trigger Scope and Obligations (§28.4.1) |
| 2 | Implement `transaction_data` in OpenID4VP requests for Dynamic Linking | PSD2 Art. 97(2), RTS Art. 5 | Payment Payload JSON Schema (TS12 Normative) (§17.14); Transactional Data HLRs (Topic 20) (§17.15) |
| 3 | Verify KB-JWT signature as SCA authentication code | RTS Art. 5 | Transaction Data Structure (§17.10) |
| 4 | Verify proof of possession of private keys (cryptographic binding) | CIR 2024/2982 Art. 5(3) | Edge Cases and Error Handling (§13.5) |
| 5 | When issuing the SCA Attestation, validate the Provider Service registration certificate, WIA, KA, requested security levels, status-maintenance periods, and KA-to-credential key binding; do not repeat WIA/KA at presentation | ARF Topics 9–10, EC TS03 | OID4VCI Issuance Flow for SCA Attestations (§17.4); RP as Credential Issuer (§17.5) |
| 6 | RP bears responsibility for authentication and validation — liability cannot be delegated | eIDAS Reg. Art. 5b(9) | Level of Assurance Verification (§13.11) |
| 7 | Evidence PSD2 RTS control over wallet-based SCA factors and PSC lifecycle controls | RTS Art. 6-9, 22-26 | SCA for Electronic Payments: Lifecycle, Flows, and Dynamic Linking (§17); Outsourcing, Delegation, and PSD2 RTS Control Boundary (§28.4.4) |
| 8 | Map EUDI SCA response to existing PSP authorisation infrastructure | — (operational requirement) | PSP Implementation Steps (§23.2.3) |
| 9 | Issue SCA attestations to customer Wallet Units via OID4VCI | TS12 | OID4VCI Issuance Flow for SCA Attestations (§17.4) |
| 10 | Monitor PSD3/PSR adoption and revalidate any profile impact against final law and technical standards | PSD3 COM(2023) 366 / 2023/0209(COD); PSR COM(2023) 367 / 2023/0210(COD) | PSD3/PSR Transition Impact (§23.2.4) |

> **PSD2 Art. 97(1)** — SCA trigger:
>
> Member States shall ensure that a payment service provider applies strong customer authentication where the payer: (a) accesses its payment account online; (b) initiates an electronic payment transaction; (c) carries out any action through a remote channel which may imply a risk in payment fraud or other abuses.

> **RTS Art. 24(2)(b)** — PSC Association trigger (fourth SCA use case):
>
> *"the association by means of a remote channel of the payment service user's identity with the personalised security credentials and with authentication devices or software is performed using strong customer authentication."*

This covers authenticator binding / authenticator enrollment — when a customer registers a new phone, adds a hardware authenticator, or re-activates credentials after loss. The EUDI Wallet can serve as the SCA method for this ceremony: an existing customer presents their PID or SCA Attestation to bootstrap a new authenticator on a new device, replacing legacy re-enrollment methods (SMS OTP, branch visit, letter-based recovery). Art. 26 extends this requirement to **renewal and re-activation** of PSCs.

**PSD2 Dynamic Linking — Art. 97(2)**:

> For the initiation of electronic payment transactions [...], Member States shall ensure that, in addition to the requirements set out in paragraph 1, strong customer authentication also includes elements which dynamically link the transaction to a specific amount and a specific payee.

The EUDI Wallet satisfies Dynamic Linking via the `transaction_data` field in the OpenID4VP request. The KB-JWT response contains a device-bound signature over the transaction hash, which constitutes the authentication code under RTS Art. 5. See §17.14 for the complete normative payload schema (TS12).

##### 28.4.2 SCA Attestation Bootstrap and Issuance

**EC-confirmed practical fulfilment model (Large Scale Pilots)**:

The European Commission's EUDIW FAQ describes the SCA attestation flow developed by Large Scale Pilots — the same model codified in TS12:

> *"Payment Service Providers issue a dedicated SCA attestation after carrying out a secure authentication of the user and linking users to their specific payment account and payment instrument. In this model, the payment service provider acts as both the issuer of the SCA attestation and the verifier. It should retain full control over the authentication decision, remaining able to authenticate the user independently. The payment service provider should remain fully responsible for validating the attestation and ensuring compliance with applicable regulations."*
>
> — [EC EUDIW FAQ — How can PSPs fulfil their obligation?](https://ec.europa.eu/digital-building-blocks/sites/spaces/EUDIGITALIDENTITYWALLET/pages/713526976/FAQ)

##### 28.4.3 SCA Presentation and Dynamic Linking

The complete flow:

| Step | Action | EC FAQ Description |
|:----:|:-------|:-------------------|
| 1 | **Registration** | User requests wallet registration for a specific payment account and payment instrument |
| 2 | **PSD2-compliant authentication** | PSP authenticates user through an existing PSD2-compliant SCA method |
| 3 | **Key generation** | Wallet generates a cryptographic key pair; private key stored securely in WSCD |
| 4 | **SCA attestation issuance** | PSP issues a device-bound SCA attestation into the user's wallet (multi-factor activation required) |
| 5 | **Transaction authentication** | Wallet presents SCA attestation with `transaction_data` for user confirmation |
| 6 | **Dynamic linking** | Confirmation is cryptographically bound to the transaction (amount + payee) |

```mermaid

  themeVariables:
    noteBkgColor: "transparent"

  sequence:
    messageAlign: left
    noteAlign: left
    actorMargin: 250
---
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant PSU as Payment Service User

    Note over PSU, PSP: Phase 1 — SCA Attestation Issuance (one-time setup)
    PSU->>PSP: Request wallet registration for payment account
    PSP->>PSU: Authenticate via PSD2-compliant bootstrap method
    PSU->>PSP: Complete bootstrap SCA (existing SCA / PID / prior SCA Attestation)
    PSP->>Wallet: Issue SCA Attestation via OID4VCI
    Wallet->>WSCD: Generate key pair, store private key
    Wallet->>PSP: Return public key binding (cnf.jwk)
    PSP->>PSP: Bind SCA Attestation to payment account + instrument
    Note right of PSP: ⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
    end

    Note over PSU, PSP: Phase 2 — SCA Presentation (per action: login, payment, TPP consent, binding, etc.)

    PSP->>Wallet: OpenID4VP request (with transaction_data for payments)
    Wallet->>PSU: Display action details for confirmation
    PSU->>Wallet: Confirm (PIN / biometric)
    Wallet->>WSCD: Sign request hash with private key
    WSCD->>Wallet: Return KB-JWT
    Wallet->>PSP: VP Token (SCA Attestation + KB-JWT)

    PSP->>PSU: Action authorised
    Note right of PSP: ⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
    end
```

> **Cross-reference**: This walkthrough mirrors the complete SCA protocol in §17. The steps below provide the bank-specific operational context; §17 contains the normative protocol specification.

<details>
<summary><strong>1. Payment Service User requests wallet registration for payment account</strong></summary>

The PSU initiates SCA Attestation enrollment by requesting to register their EUDI Wallet as an SCA method for a specific payment account and instrument. This is typically triggered via the PSP's mobile banking app or web interface — e.g., a "Register EUDI Wallet for payments" option in the security settings.

The PSP must capture the target payment account (IBAN) and payment instrument (card PAN or account reference) to bind the SCA Attestation to a specific account-instrument pair (TS12 §3.2).

</details>
<details>
<summary><strong>2. Bank/PSP authenticates PSU via a PSD2-compliant bootstrap method</strong></summary>

Before issuing an SCA Attestation into the wallet, the PSP must first verify the PSU's identity using a **PSD2-compliant bootstrap method**. That bootstrap can be the PSP's current SCA method (SMS OTP, hardware token, banking app push), an already-issued SCA Attestation from another Wallet Unit/device, or an EUDI Wallet PID presentation. PID presentation is not limited to new customers: an existing customer can also present PID as the SCA ceremony for associating a new wallet/authenticator, provided the PSP can match the PID to the existing customer relationship and accepts the SUA = SCA bridge.

This step satisfies RTS Art. 24(2)(b): the association of PSCs with a new authentication device must itself be performed using SCA. The wallet receiving the new SCA Attestation is the "new device" being onboarded; the bootstrap evidence can come from the PSP's existing SCA channel, from another already-bound Wallet Unit, or from PID presentation combined with the PSP's customer-matching policy.

</details>
<details>
<summary><strong>3. Payment Service User completes bootstrap SCA</strong></summary>

The PSU successfully completes the selected bootstrap ceremony: a legacy SCA challenge (e.g., SMS OTP, banking app push notification, hardware token), presentation of an existing SCA Attestation from another Wallet Unit/device, or PID presentation through the EUDI Wallet. This confirms the PSU is legitimately bound to the account, or has been matched to the existing/new customer record through verified PID attributes, and authorises the issuance of a new SCA credential into the target wallet.

**Failure Path:** If the bootstrap ceremony fails (wrong OTP, timeout, push rejection, invalid/revoked SCA Attestation, failed PID verification), the PSP terminates the enrollment flow and logs a `SCA_ENROLLMENT_FAILED` event.

</details>
<details>
<summary><strong>4. Bank/PSP issues SCA Attestation to EUDI Wallet via OID4VCI</strong></summary>

The PSP acts as a Credential Issuer under the OpenID for Verifiable Credential Issuance (OID4VCI) protocol. It issues a device-bound SCA Attestation containing the payment account reference, instrument identifier, and the PSP's signing key.

The attestation is an SD-JWT-VC with credential type `eu.europa.ec.eudi.sca.1` (TS12). The `cnf` claim binds the attestation to the wallet's device key — ensuring it can only be presented from the specific wallet instance that generated the key pair.

</details>
<details>
<summary><strong>5. EUDI Wallet generates key pair in WSCD, stores private key</strong></summary>

The Wallet Unit instructs the WSCD (Secure Element, TEE, or remote HSM) to generate an asymmetric key pair. The private key never leaves the WSCD — it is used exclusively for signing KB-JWTs during presentation. The public key is exported for binding.

This is the cryptographic foundation of the **possession** factor under PSD2 RTS Art. 7: the PSU possesses the device containing the WSCD with the bound private key.

</details>
<details>
<summary><strong>6. EUDI Wallet returns public key binding to Bank/PSP</strong></summary>

The wallet sends the public key to the PSP as a `cnf.jwk` claim in the OID4VCI credential response. The PSP stores this public key alongside the SCA Attestation record, enabling future verification of KB-JWT signatures.

```json
{
  "cnf": {
    "jwk": {
      "kty": "EC",
      "crv": "P-256",
      "x": "...",
      "y": "..."
    }
  }
}
```

</details>
<details>
<summary><strong>7. Bank/PSP binds SCA Attestation to payment account and instrument</strong></summary>

The PSP completes the enrollment by recording the binding: SCA Attestation ID ↔ payment account (IBAN) ↔ payment instrument ↔ public key (`cnf.jwk`). This binding enables the PSP to verify, during future transactions, that the SCA Attestation presented was issued for the specific account and instrument being used.

**Audit Telemetry:** The PSP logs a `SCA_ATTESTATION_ISSUED` event with the attestation ID, account reference (hashed), and WSCD type.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>8. Payment Service User initiates SCA-protected action</strong></summary>

The PSU triggers an action requiring SCA — any of the six triggers defined in the SCA trigger table (§28.3.3): account login (a), payment initiation (b), TPP consent (c₁), trusted beneficiary management (c₂), other remote actions (c₃), or authenticator binding (d). The PSU selects the EUDI Wallet as their preferred SCA method.

</details>
<details>
<summary><strong>9. Bank/PSP sends OpenID4VP request to EUDI Wallet</strong></summary>

The PSP constructs an OpenID4VP Authorization Request with a DCQL query requesting the SCA Attestation. For payment transactions, the request includes `transaction_data` containing the amount and payee for dynamic linking (PSD2 Art. 97(2)). For non-payment actions (login, TPP consent), `transaction_data` may be omitted or contain action-specific context.

The request is delivered via the appropriate channel: same-device intent (mobile) or cross-device QR code / `request_uri` (web).

</details>
<details>
<summary><strong>10. EUDI Wallet displays action details to Payment Service User for confirmation</strong></summary>

The Wallet UI presents the action details to the PSU for explicit confirmation. For payments, this includes the amount and payee (RTS Art. 5(1)(a) — payer awareness). For non-payment actions, the wallet displays the relying party identity and the requested attestation type.

The wallet also displays the PSP's identity from the WRPAC, enabling the PSU to verify they are authenticating to the correct institution.

</details>
<details>
<summary><strong>11. Payment Service User confirms action via PIN or biometric</strong></summary>

The PSU explicitly authorises the action by providing a second authentication factor: PIN (knowledge) or biometric (inherence). Combined with the WSCD private key (possession), this completes the multi-factor SCA requirement (PSD2 Art. 4(30): at least two of knowledge, possession, inherence).

**Failure Path:** If the PSU rejects the action or biometric verification fails, the wallet returns an error response and the PSP denies the action.

</details>
<details>
<summary><strong>12. EUDI Wallet instructs WSCD to sign request hash with private key</strong></summary>

The wallet computes a hash over the request parameters (nonce, audience, and — for payments — `transaction_data`) and submits it to the WSCD for signing. The WSCD produces an ECDSA signature using the bound private key that never leaves the secure element.

This signature constitutes the **authentication code** under RTS Art. 5: it is dynamically linked to the specific action being authenticated.

</details>
<details>
<summary><strong>13. WSCD returns KB-JWT to EUDI Wallet</strong></summary>

The WSCD returns the signed KB-JWT (Key Binding JWT) to the wallet. The KB-JWT contains the `nonce` (replay protection), `aud` (PSP identifier), `iat` (issuance timestamp), and — for payment transactions — `transaction_data_hashes` (dynamic linking).

</details>
<details>
<summary><strong>14. EUDI Wallet sends VP Token to Bank/PSP</strong></summary>

The wallet constructs a VP Token containing the SCA Attestation (SD-JWT-VC with selective disclosures) and the KB-JWT, then transmits it to the PSP's `direct_post` endpoint via the `direct_post.jwt` response mode (encrypted with the PSP's public key from the WRPAC).

</details>
<details>
<summary><strong>15. Bank/PSP verifies signature, nonce, freshness, and dynamic linking</strong></summary>

The PSP performs the complete verification pipeline:
1. **Decrypt** the JARM response using its WRPAC private key
2. **Validate** the SCA Attestation signature (issuer = self) and status (not revoked)
3. **Verify** the KB-JWT signature against the stored `cnf.jwk` public key
4. **Check** `nonce` matches the original request (anti-replay)
5. **Check** `aud` matches the PSP's identifier
6. **Validate** `iat` is within acceptable freshness window
7. **For payments:** verify `transaction_data_hashes` match the SHA-256 of the original `transaction_data` (dynamic linking — RTS Art. 5)

**Failure Path:** Any verification failure results in SCA rejection. The PSP logs the failure reason and denies the action.

</details>
<details>
<summary><strong>16. Bank/PSP confirms action authorised to Payment Service User</strong></summary>

The PSP confirms the successfully authenticated action to the PSU. For payments, this is the transaction authorisation confirmation. For account login, this establishes the authenticated session. For TPP consent, this records the SCA-backed authorisation in the PSP's consent registry.

The PSP maps the EUDI Wallet SCA result to its existing authorisation infrastructure — the wallet SCA response must produce the same downstream signals as the PSP's native SCA methods (§23.2.3).

</details>

##### 28.4.4 Outsourcing, Delegation, and PSD2 RTS Control Boundary

**No outsourcing or delegation required:**

A common PSP concern is whether accepting EUDI Wallets for SCA requires an outsourcing agreement with the Wallet Provider (triggering PSD2 Art. 19/DORA Art. 28-30 outsourcing requirements). The EC FAQ explicitly addresses this:

> *"Outsourcing agreements between payment service providers and wallets providers are not required under Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 for the implementation of the wallets for SCA. Where payment service providers act as both issuer of the SCA attestation and verifier, they should retain full control over the authentication decision and remain fully responsible for validating the attestation and ensuring compliance with applicable regulations. In this model, the wallets act as a secure carrier of the attested information. Given that payment service providers are responsible for issuing and relying upon attestations for SCA, a delegation of the authentication to a third party does not take place."*
>
> — [EC EUDIW FAQ — Are outsourcing agreements necessary?](https://ec.europa.eu/digital-building-blocks/sites/spaces/EUDIGITALIDENTITYWALLET/pages/713526976/FAQ)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    PSP["`**PSP**
    Issues SCA Attestation
    Sends OpenID4VP request
    Verifies response
    Makes authentication decision`"]

    WU["`**Wallet Unit**
    Secure carrier
    Renders transaction
    Invokes local user auth
    Produces presentation`"]

    SEC["`**Wallet Security Evidence**
    Issuance WIA / KA chain
    WSCA / WSCD policy
    Holder-bound key`"]

    PROOF["`**SCA Proof**
    SCA Attestation
    KB-JWT
    amr
    jti
    transaction_data_hashes`"]

    RTS["`**PSD2 RTS Properties**
    PSC confidentiality
    Secure association
    Factor independence
    Authentication code
    Dynamic linking`"]

    DECISION["`**PSP Decision**
    Accept
    Step up
    Reject`"]

    PSP -->|"issuer/verifier model"| WU
    WU --> SEC
    WU --> PROOF
    SEC --> RTS
    PROOF --> RTS
    RTS --> PSP
    PSP --> DECISION

    WU -. "not delegated authenticator in this model" .-> PSP
```

This is significant, but it should be read precisely. The FAQ resolves the **delegation** question for the TS12 SCA Attestation model: the Wallet acts as a **secure carrier**, not as the party making the authentication decision. The PSP issues the attestation, the Wallet stores and presents it, and the PSP verifies it. On that model, the Wallet Provider is not the PSP's outsourced authentication provider.

:::note[Boundary of the EC FAQ Clarification]
The EC FAQ is not a blanket PSD2 RTS certification of every Wallet Unit, local PIN, biometric subsystem, or pass-through wallet implementation. It confirms that no outsourcing agreement is required where the PSP remains both issuer and verifier of the SCA Attestation. The PSP must still evidence that the wallet-based flow satisfies the RTS requirements for confidentiality, integrity, secure association, factor independence, authentication-code generation, and dynamic linking.
:::

**PSD2 RTS control model — "ensure" does not mean "physically operate every factor":**

The PSD2 RTS uses an assurance-and-control formulation. It does not require the PSP to physically operate every low-level component in the user's device, but it does require the PSP to **ensure** the relevant security properties. Articles 22-26 require confidentiality and integrity of personalised security credentials, secure creation, secure delivery, secure association with the payment service user, and secure renewal/reactivation. Articles 6-9 require mitigations for knowledge, possession, and inherence elements, plus independence between factors. Articles 4-5 require a unique authentication code and dynamic linking for payment transactions.

That distinction matters for wallet-local PINs and biometrics. A PSP should not treat an unmanaged phone lock, generic wallet unlock, or opaque biometric prompt as an RTS-compliant SCA factor merely because the PSP receives a successful wallet response. If the wallet-local PIN or biometric is counted as part of SCA, the PSP needs a defensible evidence chain showing that the factor was enrolled, protected, invoked, and reported under a certified wallet profile or equivalent control framework.

In the TS12 model, the PSP-provided personalised security credential is the **SCA Attestation** and its account/payment-instrument binding. The Wallet Unit's local authentication ceremony unlocks use of the holder-bound key. The PSP does not need the user's biometric template or wallet PIN value, but it does need assurance that the wallet can only produce the KB-JWT after an acceptable multi-factor ceremony and that the resulting proof is bound to the right user, Wallet Unit, account/instrument, and transaction.

| RTS control question | What the PSP must be able to evidence | EUDI Wallet / TS12 evidence surface |
|:---------------------|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------|
| **PSC confidentiality and integrity** | Credentials and authentication codes are protected throughout authentication; secrets are not stored or exposed in plain text | SCA Attestation signature, encrypted presentation response, KA-admitted non-exportable key policy at issuance, secure Wallet storage/certification, and PSP-side verification logs |
| **Secure creation, delivery, and activation** | The SCA Attestation and associated authentication device/software are created, delivered, and activated through secure channels | OID4VCI issuance after existing PSD2 SCA or PID-based SCA, proof-of-possession at issuance, activation under the wallet's multi-factor ceremony |
| **Secure association with the PSU** | Only the legitimate payment service user is associated with the credential, device, and software; remote association itself uses SCA | PSP-controlled enrolment session, PID or existing-SCA bootstrap, account/instrument binding, `cnf.jwk`, attestation revocation lifecycle |
| **Knowledge / inherence factor quality** | PIN or biometric factors are protected against disclosure, spoofing, and unauthorised use | Certified Wallet Unit behaviour, rulebook constraints, `amr` values, biometric/PIN policy evidence; not a generic OS unlock unless the control framework covers it |
| **Possession and factor independence** | Compromise of one factor does not compromise the others, especially on a multi-purpose device | Holder-bound private key admitted by issuance KA in WSCD/WSCA or an accepted secure cryptographic environment, requested User-authentication level, isolated key use, and replay controls |
| **Authentication code and dynamic linking** | The accepted authentication code is unique, fresh, and specific to amount and payee | KB-JWT `jti`, `nonce`, `aud`, `iat`, `transaction_data_hashes`, PSP recomputation of transaction hashes |

The correct compliance position is therefore not "the PSP merely validates." It is: the PSP retains the authentication decision, issues and verifies the SCA Attestation, and relies on certified wallet evidence to satisfy the RTS properties it must ensure. If a wallet provider or pass-through wallet operator instead **supplies or verifies SCA elements** or makes the effective authentication decision outside this issuer/verifier model, the ordinary outsourcing and third-party-risk analysis returns. This reconciles the EC FAQ with the EBA's [digital-wallet SCA Q&As](https://eba.europa.eu/publications-and-media/press-releases/eba-clarifies-application-strong-customer-authentication): pass-through wallet operators that provide or verify SCA elements require outsourcing analysis, while the TS12 issuer/verifier model keeps the authentication decision with the PSP.

> **⚠️ Outsourcing distinction**: While the Wallet Provider is *not* an outsourced authentication provider, an RP *intermediary* (Art. 5b(10)) that handles wallet verification on behalf of the PSP *is* an ICT third-party service provider under DORA Art. 28. See §23.4 for the DORA implications.

##### 28.4.5 Accept vs Issue: Why Issuance Is De Facto Required

**The "accept" vs. "issue" question — is SCA Attestation issuance mandatory?**

A subtle but critical regulatory nuance: eIDAS Art. 5f(2) requires PSPs to **accept** EUDI Wallets — a relying party obligation. It does not contain a "shall issue" clause for SCA Attestations. No provision in eIDAS 2.0 explicitly mandates that PSPs act as Credential Issuers under OID4VCI. The EC FAQ describes the SCA Attestation issuance model as the recommended compliance path ("Payment Service Providers **issue** a dedicated SCA attestation"), but FAQ guidance is not legally operative.

This creates a potential wiggle room that PSPs may attempt to exploit:

| Argument | Counter |
|:---------|:--------|
| "We accept the wallet, but we haven't built issuance yet" | Art. 5f(2) requires acceptance **"upon the voluntary request of the user."** If a user requests wallet-based SCA and the PSP cannot provide it because it hasn't implemented issuance, the user's right is frustrated — the PSP has failed to accept. |
| "We accept the wallet for PID verification (CDD) but not for SCA" | Art. 5f(2) applies to every SCA trigger under PSD2 Art. 97. Selective acceptance violates the regulation. |
| "We'll issue attestations later — the regulation doesn't specify when" | The "upon request" language sets the trigger: when a user requests wallet SCA, the PSP must be ready. The deadline is 24 December 2027 — by that date, both acceptance and the issuance infrastructure enabling it must be operational. |

**The logical chain that makes issuance *de facto* mandatory:**

1. **Art. 5f(2):** PSPs must accept the EUDI Wallet for SCA, upon user request
2. **TS12 model:** Wallet-based SCA requires an SCA Attestation issued by the PSP into the wallet
3. **No alternative model exists:** No specification describes a wallet SCA flow that does not require PSP-issued attestations
4. **Therefore:** To *accept* the wallet for SCA, the PSP must have the capability to *issue* SCA Attestations — making issuance a necessary precondition of the acceptance obligation

> **Timing:** Issuance is not triggered at account opening or authenticator binding — it is triggered **when the user requests to use the EUDI Wallet for SCA**. At that moment, the PSP must offer enrollment (the Phase 1 issuance flow above). PSPs have no obligation to proactively push SCA Attestations to all customers — but they must have the infrastructure ready to issue on demand by the December 2027 deadline.

> **Cross-reference:** The Dutch PA's Dispute 4 (§28.9) argued that PSPs "are not required to issue EAAs." This is technically correct at the eIDAS level but practically irrelevant: the SCA Attestation model — endorsed by the EC FAQ, piloted by EWC/NOBID LSPs, and codified in TS12 — is the only specified compliance path. A PSP deviating from this model bears the burden of demonstrating that its alternative satisfies both eIDAS and PSD2/RTS requirements.

##### 28.4.6 PSD2/RTS Wrapper: Lifecycle, Monitoring, Exemptions, Evidence, and TPP Parity

TS12 answers the Wallet protocol question; it does not exhaust the PSP compliance checklist. The PSP still has to run the surrounding PSD2/RTS controls that determine when SCA is required, when an exemption is defensible, what evidence must be retained, how disputes are defended, and how TPP-mediated flows remain non-discriminatory.

**A. Payment-instrument and PSC lifecycle controls**

Wallet-based SCA should be mapped against both PSD2 payment-instrument duties and RTS personalised-security-credential controls. This prevents two common mistakes: treating every token/enrolment event as only a payment transaction, or treating the Wallet Unit as a generic unmanaged phone lock.

| Lifecycle surface | PSD2/RTS basis | Wallet-specific checklist impact |
|:------------------|:---------------|:---------------------------------|
| **Payment instrument issuance / token creation** | PSD2 Art. 70; [EBA Q&A 2020_5622](https://www.eba.europa.eu/single-rule-book-qa/qna/view/publicId/2020_5622) | Verify the PSU is the rightful user of the underlying account/card, safeguard PSCs, avoid unsolicited instruments, support blocking/unblocking, and record issuer-side decision evidence. |
| **Remote enrolment / card or account binding to wallet** | PSD2 Art. 97(1)(c); RTS Art. 24(2)(b) | Apply SCA when the payer remotely associates identity, PSCs, authentication devices, or software. PID presentation, prior SCA Attestation, or existing PSP SCA can bootstrap the binding where the PSP can match the PSU. |
| **Token or SCA Attestation replacement** | RTS Art. 24 and Art. 26; [EBA Q&A 2022_6464](https://www.eba.europa.eu/single-rule-book-qa/qna/view/publicId/2022_6464) | Treat replacement that creates a new token/credential and binds it to a device/user as a fresh association event; do not classify it as mere background maintenance simply because the issuer or token service initiates the replacement. |
| **Loss, theft, misappropriation, and blocking** | PSD2 Art. 69-70; RTS Art. 26 | Provide user notification/blocking channels, revoke or suspend affected attestations, and preserve the timeline needed to separate user notification, PSP action, and subsequent attempts. |
| **Credential renewal and reactivation** | RTS Art. 26 | Use SCA for remote renewal/reactivation of PSCs or authentication software, and log the bootstrap method, device binding, and revocation status. |

**B. Transaction monitoring and exemption governance**

RTS Art. 2 transaction monitoring is not optional telemetry. PSPs must have mechanisms to detect unauthorised or fraudulent payment transactions. The EBA clarified in [Q&A 2018_4090](https://eba.europa.eu/single-rule-book-qa/qna/view/publicId/2018_4090) that the general Art. 2 monitoring requirement does not by itself require real-time monitoring, but the RTS Art. 18 Transaction Risk Analysis exemption does: a PSP relying on TRA must perform real-time risk analysis before the transaction is authorised.

That distinction is important for Wallet integration. A valid Wallet SCA proof is one input to fraud control; it is not a substitute for the monitoring and exemption decision.

| RTS exemption / control | Wallet effect | Evidence to retain |
|:------------------------|:--------------|:-------------------|
| **Account-information access exemption** (RTS Art. 10 / 10a) | Do not force unnecessary Wallet SCA where the account-access exemption applies, including AISP access where the amended RTS conditions are met. | Exemption basis, consent/access context, AISP identity, last SCA time where relevant. |
| **Contactless and unattended-terminal exemptions** (RTS Art. 11-12) | Usually outside the online Wallet SCA path, but card issuers should keep the exemption logic separate from TS12 remote SCA. | Terminal type, amount/counter limits, payment instrument state, fallback decision. |
| **Trusted beneficiaries** (RTS Art. 13) | Adding/amending/deleting a trusted beneficiary requires SCA; the Wallet can be the user-chosen SCA method. Later payments to that beneficiary may be exempt if conditions remain satisfied. | Trusted-list change event, SCA proof for list management, payee identity, timestamp, subsequent exemption flag. |
| **Recurring / fixed-amount series** (RTS Art. 14) | Initial setup or amendment needs SCA and dynamic linking; subsequent same-payee/same-amount transactions may be exempt. | Initial dynamic-linking proof, mandate/series identifier, amount/payee invariants, change history. |
| **Same-user transfers** (RTS Art. 15) | Exemption depends on payer/payee account ownership and PSP policy; Wallet SCA is still needed if the exemption is not applied. | Ownership match evidence, account identifiers, exemption decision. |
| **Low-value remote payments** (RTS Art. 16) | PSP may exempt low-value transactions within cumulative thresholds, but must step up to Wallet SCA when thresholds or risk controls require it. | Amount, cumulative count/value since last SCA, risk score, step-up result. |
| **Secure corporate payment processes** (RTS Art. 17) | Corporate wallet/mandate flows should not be mixed with consumer SCA Attestation assumptions; document the corporate-process exemption separately. | Corporate process approval, mandate/role proof, audit trail, NCA acceptance where applicable. |
| **Transaction Risk Analysis** (RTS Art. 18) | Credential/holder-binding results, authoritative Wallet Solution status, issuer-retained WIA/KA issuance assurance, payer context, payee risk, and VoP/IBAN-name results feed the real-time TRA decision. If risk is too high, route to Wallet SCA or block. | Real-time score, model version, input signals, fraud-rate tier, exemption/step-up/block outcome. |

**C. Evidence, traceability, and liability**

PSD2 Art. 72 makes evidence a first-class compliance surface: where the PSU denies authorising a transaction or claims incorrect execution, the PSP must prove that the transaction was authenticated, accurately recorded, entered in the accounts, and not affected by a technical breakdown or other deficiency. RTS Art. 29 adds the traceability layer: payment transactions and interactions with PSUs, PSPs, merchants, and other entities must be traceable ex post, including detailed transaction logging.

For Wallet SCA, the PSP evidence package should include at least:

| Evidence object | Why it matters |
|:----------------|:---------------|
| SCA Attestation identifier and status at verification time | Proves which PSP-issued credential was accepted and whether it was valid. |
| Issuance-assurance reference + presentation holder-binding result | Shows that the PSP issued against its provider-certificate/WIA/KA policy and later verified possession of the bound key; raw WIA/KA is not a presentation artifact. |
| `amr`, factor category interpretation, and local-factor assurance source | Shows which SCA elements were counted and why they were acceptable under RTS Art. 6-9. |
| KB-JWT `jti`, `nonce`, `aud`, `iat`, and signature result | Shows uniqueness, freshness, relying-party targeting, and replay resistance. |
| `transaction_data` and `transaction_data_hashes` recomputation | Shows dynamic linking to amount and payee for remote payment transactions. |
| Exemption decision, if SCA was not applied | Shows which RTS exemption was used and the inputs supporting that decision. |
| PISP/AISP request context, where relevant | Shows the ASPSP received and processed the TPP-mediated request correctly. |
| Technical-deficiency and incident state | Shows whether outage, latency, misrouting, or wallet/certificate-status failure affected the transaction. |

:::warning[Do Not Treat SCA Success As the Whole Liability Answer]
The [EBA's 2024 fraud opinion](https://www.eba.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2024-04/363649ff-27b4-4210-95a6-0a87c9e21272/Opinion%20on%20new%20types%20of%20payment%20fraud%20and%20possible%20mitigations.pdf) highlights a regulatory concern with treating every SCA-authenticated payment as automatically authorised, especially in social-engineering and authorised-push-payment fraud scenarios. Design dispute handling around the full Art. 72 evidence package and the Art. 73-74 liability framework, not around a single "SCA passed" flag.
:::

RTS Art. 29 does **not** by itself establish a universal fixed retention period for all Wallet SCA evidence. [EBA Q&A 2022_6526](https://www.eba.europa.eu/single-rule-book-qa/qna/view/publicId/2022_6526) confirms the record-keeping duty and states that applicable Union and national retention periods apply. PSPs should therefore align Wallet SCA logs with payment-service, AML, DORA, GDPR, and national limitation-period requirements, using minimised and hashed artefacts where raw transaction or identity data is not needed.

**D. TPP / open-banking parity and common secure communication**

Wallet SCA must also work in PIS/AIS journeys. PSD2 Art. 97(5) and RTS Art. 30 require AISPs and PISPs to be able to rely on the ASPSP authentication procedures provided to the PSU. The EBA's RTS implementation opinion ties this to the dedicated-interface and secure-communication requirements in RTS Art. 30-36.

Operationally, the ASPSP should ensure that:

| Open-banking requirement | Wallet-specific implementation consequence |
|:-------------------------|:-------------------------------------------|
| PISPs/AISPs can rely on ASPSP authentication procedures | The Wallet SCA option must be reachable in TPP-mediated journeys, not only in the bank's first-party web/app flow. |
| PISP/AISP identity is authenticated through the PSD2 certificate/register stack | Keep the PSD2/open-banking `QWAC` / `QSealC` / `QCStatement` stack separate from Wallet `WRPAC` / `WRPRC`; both may be needed in one journey. |
| Dedicated interface is not an obstacle | Do not make Wallet SCA slower, less available, or less exemption-capable for PIS/AIS than native ASPSP SCA. |
| Consent and request context remain auditable | Store the TPP request, ASPSP SCA result, exemption decision, and response path; do not require the ASPSP to police TPP consent beyond PSD2's allocation of responsibilities. |
| Secure communication remains traceable | Preserve transaction number, timestamps, request identifiers, and routing metadata sufficient to reconstruct the TPP-mediated flow. |

This is why the SCA-exemption dispute in §28.9 should be read narrowly. The unresolved part is not whether PSPs must operate transaction monitoring, traceability, or secure communication today; they already must. The open part is how future PSR/PSD3 RTS will standardise Wallet-specific parity for TRA exemptions, TPP journeys, and evidence packages.

#### 28.5 CDD/KYC and Identity Assurance

##### 28.5.1 Customer Due Diligence (AML/KYC)

🔴 **Mandatory** — All banks and PSPs subject to AMLD/AMLR CDD requirements

Banks and PSPs subject to AMLD must implement EUDI Wallet PID presentation as a CDD onboarding channel. This replaces or supplements traditional identity verification methods (video-ident, PostIdent, document scanning).

| # | Obligation | Regulatory Basis | DR-0002 Reference |
|:-:|:-----------|:-----------------|:------------------|
| 1 | Accept PID presentation for CDD identity verification | AMLD Art. 13; Recital 62 | Customer Due Diligence (CDD) Flow (§24.1) |
| 2 | Request only CDD-necessary PID attributes | GDPR Art. 5(1)(c), eIDAS Reg. Art. 5b(3) | Customer Due Diligence (CDD) Flow (§24.1) |
| 3 | Perform AML/Sanctions/PEP screening against verified PID attributes | AMLD Art. 13(1)(a) | Customer Due Diligence (CDD) Flow, Phase 2 AML Screening (§24.1) |
| 4 | Perform Enhanced Due Diligence if triggered (high-risk indicators) | AMLD Art. 18 | Customer Due Diligence (CDD) Flow, Phase 3 Enhanced Due Diligence (§24.1) |
| 5 | Accept PID at LoA High as satisfying CDD identification requirement | AMLD Art. 13 + eIDAS Reg. Art. 5a(11) | Customer Due Diligence (CDD) Flow (§24.1); Level of Assurance Verification (§13.11) |

> **⚠️ Critical rule**: Proof of Age (`age_over_18` and optional `age_over_NN`) is not customer identity evidence and cannot replace AML/CDD. Use the applicable PID and downstream CDD controls for that decision. Keep any separate lawful age-only use distinct. See §21.1.3 and §21.1.6.

**CDD attribute set**: The minimum PID attributes required for CDD under AMLD Art. 13 typically include:

| PID Attribute | AMLD Purpose | DCQL Claim ID |
|:-------------|:-------------|:-------------|
| `family_name` | Identity verification | `urn:eudi:pid:1:family_name` |
| `given_name` | Identity verification | `urn:eudi:pid:1:given_name` |
| `birthdate` | Identity verification, age threshold calculation where legally justified | `urn:eudi:pid:1:birthdate` |
| `nationalities` | Sanctions/PEP screening | `urn:eudi:pid:1:nationalities` |
| `personal_administrative_number` | Jurisdiction-dependent registry matching, where issued and legally needed | `urn:eudi:pid:1:personal_administrative_number` |
| `address.*` | Address verification (if address attestation unavailable) | `urn:eudi:pid:1:address.country`, `address.locality`, `address.postal_code`, `address.formatted` |

Register these attributes as a distinct intended use ("CDD onboarding") in the RP registration. Do not bundle CDD attributes with SCA attributes in a single declaration — this violates purpose limitation.

##### 28.5.2 Identity Matching (CIR 2025/846)

🔴 **Mandatory** — All banks and PSPs accepting PID presentations

When a user presents PID via EUDI Wallet, the PSP must match the presented identity to an existing customer record (or create a new one). CIR 2025/846 imposes specific obligations on this process:

| # | Obligation | Regulatory Basis | DR-0002 Reference |
|:-:|:-----------|:-----------------|:------------------|
| 1 | Use mandatory PID attributes (family_name, given_name, birth_date, birth_place, nationality) for identity matching | CIR 2025/846 Art. 2(3); CIR 2024/2977 Annex §1 | Cross-Border Presentation Overview (§25.1) |
| 2 | Handle orthographic variations (transliteration, hyphenation, blank spaces, concatenation) | CIR 2025/846 Art. 2(6) | Language Handling in Consent Screens (§25.3) |
| 3 | Inform user of successful match outcome, whether matched to existing record or registered as new user | CIR 2025/846 Art. 3(1-2) | Cross-Border Attribute Compatibility (§25.4) |
| 4 | Inform user when identity matching fails and provide alternative methods | CIR 2025/846 Art. 4(1) | Non-EU Credential Recognition (§25.5) |
| 5 | Retain identity matching logs for 6–12 months (values, timestamps, documentation, outcomes) | CIR 2025/846 Art. 5(1-3) | Identity Matching Normalisation (CIR 2025/846) (§25.6) |

**Bank-specific application**: Identity matching is where PID presentation meets the bank's existing customer record system. Key challenges for PSPs:

- **Cross-border transliteration**: A customer registered as "Müller" in Germany may present a Greek-issued PID with "MUELLER" — CIR 2025/846 Art. 2(6) requires the matching process to handle this gracefully.
- **Multi-name conventions**: PID `family_name` may contain compound names with varying hyphenation or concatenation rules across MSs (e.g., "García-López" vs "Garcia Lopez").
- **Existing records**: Banks already have customer records from traditional onboarding. The matching process must link incoming EUDI PID to these existing records without creating duplicates.
- **Failure transparency**: When matching fails (e.g., name mismatch due to name change not yet reflected in PID), the PSP must inform the user and offer alternatives — not silently reject.

> **⚠️ Log retention**: The 6-12 month retention period for matching logs intersects with AMLR record-keeping obligations (which may require longer retention for CDD records). PSPs should align identity matching log retention with their existing AML record-keeping policies, applying the longer of the two periods.

##### 28.5.3 Supplementary Identity Verification: Portrait, PAD, and Capture Integrity

🟡 **Conditional / risk-based** — Banks and PSPs performing remote AML/CDD onboarding where additional live-person assurance is justified

Banks face a unique tension: eIDAS 2.0 and the Wallet trust chain can already provide a **high-assurance upstream identity result**, while AMLR still requires the RP to manage fraud, mule, coercion, and onboarding risk in its own channel. Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/798 sharpens this distinction by formalising a harmonised remote-onboarding path in which a wallet user may be onboarded with an eID means at **LoA substantial** plus additional remote proofing steps that together satisfy **LoA high**. In other words: the Wallet/PID may already arrive at the RP with a stronger upstream identity-proofing pedigree than the earlier 2024/2025 text alone made explicit.

That means three distinct "binding" questions should be kept separate:

| Layer | What is being bound | Who is responsible | Typical evidence |
|:------|:--------------------|:-------------------|:-----------------|
| **1. Upstream onboarding / issuance binding** | Real-world person ↔ PID ↔ Wallet Unit / user device | PID provider / wallet onboarding stack | Issuer identity proofing, Wallet issuance controls, applicable Authentic Source verification through ETSI TS 119 478 where used, CIR 2026/798 / CIR 2024/2977 compliance |
| **2. Presentation-time holder binding** | Presented credential ↔ current Wallet Unit control | RP / intermediary verifier | KB-JWT or DeviceAuth, issuer signature, credential status, session binding, and authoritative Wallet Solution policy where applicable |
| **3. RP-side live-person binding** | Current presenter ↔ the human physically in front of the camera / onboarding session | RP | Selfie, video-ident, `portrait` comparison, PAD, operator review |

For many RP use cases, **layers 1 and 2 are enough**. If the RP trusts the issuer's proofing, validates the trust chain, checks revocation, and verifies holder/device binding, it does **not** automatically need the optional `portrait` attribute. Portrait/PAD becomes relevant when the RP wants an additional **session-local live-person check** beyond the upstream trust it already receives.

The July 2025 **ANSSI/BSI joint paper** is useful here because it breaks remote identity proofing into three separate verification goals: **biometric genuineness**, **document authenticity**, and **face matching**. For RP-side supplementary checks, that means a `portrait`/selfie step addresses only part of the problem. It can strengthen the link between the current presenter and the PID holder, but it does not by itself prove that any additional document shown to the camera is genuine, current, or actually in the applicant's possession.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    INPUT["`**Inputs**
    Live presenter
    PID portrait / attributes
    Optional physical identity document`"]

    subgraph CAPTURE["`**Capture**`"]
        FACE["`Face capture
        Selfie / video stream`"]
        DOC["`Document capture
        Camera capture or NFC chip read`"]
    end

    subgraph PROCESS["`**Processing**`"]
        BIO["`Biometric genuineness
        PAD / liveness / anti-spoofing`"]
        AUTH["`Document authenticity
        Chip validation / document checks`"]
        MATCH["`Face matching
        Presenter ↔ portrait / document photo`"]
        CTRL["`Controls
        Challenge-response
        Tamper checks
        Policy gates`"]
    end

    DECISION["`**Decision**
    Allow
    Step-up
    Reject / review`"]

    INPUT --> FACE
    INPUT --> DOC
    FACE --> BIO
    FACE --> MATCH
    DOC --> AUTH
    DOC --> MATCH
    BIO --> CTRL
    AUTH --> CTRL
    MATCH --> CTRL
    CTRL --> DECISION

    style INPUT text-align:left
    style FACE text-align:left
    style DOC text-align:left
    style BIO text-align:left
    style AUTH text-align:left
    style MATCH text-align:left
    style CTRL text-align:left
    style DECISION text-align:left
```
